title.zh: 卷一百五十八 列傳第一百〇八: 武元衡 鄭餘慶 韋貫之
title.en: Volume 158 Biographies 108: Wu Yuanheng, Zheng Yuqing, Wei Guanzhi
title.raw: 卷一百五十八 列傳第一百〇八: 武元衡 鄭餘慶 韋貫之 Volume 158 Biographies 108: Wu Yuanheng, Zheng Yuqing, Wei Guanzhi

sentences.zh: 武元衡，字伯蒼，河南緱氏人。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanheng, courtesy name Bocang, was a native of Gouyi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng, whose courtesy name was Bocang, came from Gouyi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖載德，天后從父弟，官至湖州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zaide was the Empress Wu's younger cousin on her father's side and reached the office of prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zaide was a paternal cousin of Empress Wu and rose to serve as prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖平一，善屬文，終考功員外郎、修文館學士，事在《逸人傳》。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pingyi was skilled at literary composition and ended as a supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and a scholar of the Hall for Cultivating Literature; his story is in the Biographies of Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pingyi was a gifted writer who ultimately held posts in the Ministry of Personnel and at the Hall for Cultivating Literature; his life is recorded in the Biographies of Recluses.

sentences.zh: 父就，殿中侍御史，以元衡貴，追贈吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Jiu was an attendant censor in the palace, and because of Yuanheng's eminence was posthumously awarded the title of vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiu had served as a palace censor and, owing to Yuanheng's distinction, was posthumously ennobled as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 元衡進士登第，累辟使府，至監察御史。

translations.literal: Yuanheng passed the jinshi examination, was repeatedly summoned to commissioners' staffs, and reached the post of investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, Yuanheng served on several military commissioners' staffs before being appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 後為華原縣令。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Huayuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed magistrate of Huayuan County.

sentences.zh: 時畿輔有鎮軍督將恃恩矜功者，多撓吏民。

translations.literal: At the time in the capital region there were generals of frontier armies who relied on favor and boasted of merit, and they often interfered with officials and the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital region at that time, frontier army generals who traded on imperial favor and their own achievements often bullied local officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 元衡苦之，乃稱病去官。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was distressed by this and therefore pleaded illness and resigned his office.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed by the situation, Yuanheng pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 放情事外，沈浮宴詠者久之。

translations.literal: He let his feelings roam beyond official matters and for a long time drifted among banquets and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He turned away from office and for a long while lived amid feasting and verse.

sentences.zh: 德宗知其才，召授比部員外郎。

translations.literal: Dezong knew his talent and summoned him to appoint him supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, aware of his ability, recalled him and appointed him supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 一歲，遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: Within one year he was promoted to left bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was promoted to director in the left bureau of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時以詳整稱重。

translations.literal: At the time he was esteemed for his thoroughness and orderliness.
translations.idiomatic: He was then widely respected for his meticulous, orderly conduct.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十年，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of the Zhenyuan reign he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 20 he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 嘗因延英對罷，德宗目送之，指示左右曰：「元衡真宰相器也。」

translations.literal: Once, after concluding an audience at Yanying Hall, Dezong watched him leave and said to those nearby, "Yuanheng truly has the makings of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Once, as an audience at Yanying Hall ended, Dezong watched him go and told his attendants, "Yuanheng truly has the makings of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，以病不親政事。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, he did not personally attend to state affairs because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, illness kept him from handling government in person.

sentences.zh: 王叔文等使其黨以權利誘元衡，元衡拒之。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen and others had their faction try to entice Yuanheng with power and profit, but Yuanheng refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen and his allies sent their followers to tempt Yuanheng with power and profit, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 時奉德宗山陵，元衡為儀仗使。

translations.literal: At the time they were conducting Dezong's imperial tomb observances, and Yuanheng served as commissioner of ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was observing rites for Dezong's burial, and Yuanheng served as commissioner of ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 監察御史劉禹錫，叔文之黨也，求充儀仗判官。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Liu Yuxi, a member of Shuwen's faction, sought appointment as administrative aide to the ceremonial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Liu Yuxi, a member of Shuwen's faction, asked to serve as administrative aide on the ceremonial staff.

sentences.zh: 元衡不與，其黨滋不悅。

translations.literal: Yuanheng would not grant it, and their faction grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng refused, and their faction grew still more hostile.

sentences.zh: 數日，罷元衡為右庶子。

translations.literal: Within days Yuanheng was removed and made right guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Yuanheng was demoted to right guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，始冊為皇太子，元衡贊引，因識之。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended the throne and the heir apparent was first enfeoffed, Yuanheng served as usher at the ceremony and thus came to be known to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne and first invested the crown prince, Yuanheng directed the ceremony and thereby came to his notice.

sentences.zh: 及登極，復拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: When he assumed the throne, Yuanheng was again appointed vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xianzong was enthroned, Yuanheng was again made vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 持平無私，綱條悉舉，人甚稱重。

translations.literal: He was even-handed and impartial, enforced every regulation, and people greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Impartial and even-handed, he enforced the full body of regulations, and the court held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 尋遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和二年正月，拜門下侍郎、平章事，賜金紫，兼判戶部事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Yuanhe, he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery, chief councilor, granted the gold-and-purple insignia, and concurrently given charge of revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanhe 2 he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and chief councilor, awarded the gold-and-purple insignia, and concurrently placed in charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 上為太子時，知其進退守正，及是用為宰相，甚禮信之。

translations.literal: When the emperor had been crown prince, he had known Yuanheng's upright conduct in advancing and withdrawing; now he used him as chief minister and treated him with great courtesy and trust.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince Xianzong had known Yuanheng's steadfast integrity; now he made him chief minister and treated him with exceptional trust and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 初，浙西節度李錡請入覲，乃拜為右僕射，令入朝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Qi, military commissioner of Zhexi, had requested permission to come to court, and he was therefore appointed right vice director of the Secretariat and ordered to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Qi, military commissioner of Zhexi, had asked leave to come to court and was appointed right vice director of the Secretariat with orders to attend.

sentences.zh: 既而又稱疾，請至歲暮。

translations.literal: Then he again pleaded illness and asked to delay until year's end.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness again and asked to postpone his arrival until the end of the year.

sentences.zh: 上問宰臣，鄭絪請如錡奏。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers; Zheng Yin requested that Li Qi's petition be granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the chief ministers, and Zheng Yin urged that Li Qi's request be granted.

sentences.zh: 元衡曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Yuanheng said, "That cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng said, "That cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 且錡自請入朝，詔既許之，即又稱疾，是可否在錡。

translations.literal: Moreover, Li Qi himself asked to come to court, and once the edict had permitted it, he again pleaded illness—so whether he comes or not lies with Li Qi alone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi had himself asked to attend court and the throne had already assented; now he pleads illness again—so whether he comes or stays away is entirely up to Li Qi.

sentences.zh: 今陛下新臨大寶，天下屬耳目，若使奸臣得遂其私，則威令從茲去矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has newly assumed the great mandate; the whole realm is watching. If a treacherous minister is allowed to have his way, imperial authority will slip away from this moment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just assumed the throne and all eyes are upon you. If a treacherous minister is allowed his whim, imperial authority will be lost from this day forward.

sentences.zh: 」上以為然，遽追之。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct and immediately ordered Li Qi recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and at once ordered Li Qi recalled.

sentences.zh: 錡果計窮而反。

translations.literal: Li Qi, his stratagems exhausted, turned back as expected.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, his schemes exhausted, turned back as expected.

sentences.zh: 先是，高崇文平蜀，因授以節度使。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Gao Chongwen had pacified Shu, he was therefore appointed military commissioner there.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Gao Chongwen pacified Shu, he had been appointed military commissioner of the region.

sentences.zh: 崇文理軍有法，而不知州縣之政。

translations.literal: Chongwen disciplined the army effectively but did not understand the government of prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen governed the army with discipline but knew little of civil administration in the prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 上難其代者，乃以元衡代崇文，拜檢校吏部尚書，兼門下侍郎、平章事，充劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor found it hard to replace him, so Yuanheng was sent to succeed Chongwen, appointed acting minister of personnel, concurrently vice director of the Chancellery and chief councilor, and made military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Finding it difficult to replace him, the court sent Yuanheng to succeed Chongwen as acting minister of personnel, concurrently vice director of the Chancellery and chief councilor, and military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 將行，上御安福門以臨慰之。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the emperor came to the Gate of Peace and Felicity to see him off and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure the emperor came to the Gate of Peace and Felicity to see him off and offer encouragement.

sentences.zh: 高崇文既發成都，盡載其軍資、金帛、帟幕、伎樂、工巧以行。

translations.literal: After Gao Chongwen had left Chengdu, he carried off all his military stores, gold and silk, tents and curtains, musicians, artisans, and craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Chongwen left Chengdu he removed all his military stores, gold and silk, tents and hangings, musicians, and skilled craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 元衡至，則庶事節約，務以便人。

translations.literal: When Yuanheng arrived, he practiced economy in all affairs and strove to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanheng arrived he practiced economy in all matters and strove to ease life for the people.

sentences.zh: 比三年，公私稍濟。

translations.literal: After about three years, public and private affairs had gradually recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Within about three years public and private affairs had gradually improved.

sentences.zh: 撫蠻夷，約束明具，不輒生事。

translations.literal: He pacified the barbarian tribes, set clear constraints, and did not lightly provoke incidents.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the frontier peoples, laid down clear rules, and did not lightly provoke trouble.

sentences.zh: 重慎端謹，雖淡於接物，而開府極一時之選。

translations.literal: Serious, cautious, and proper, though reserved in social dealings, his staff appointments were the finest of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Grave, cautious, and proper—though cool in personal relations—his staff appointments ranked among the finest of the age.

sentences.zh: 八年，徵還。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was recalled to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至駱谷，重拜門下侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: At Lu Valley he was again appointed vice director of the Chancellery and chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At Lu Valley he was again appointed vice director of the Chancellery and chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 時李吉甫、李絳情不相葉，各以事理曲直於上前。

translations.literal: At the time Li Jifu and Li Jiang were on bad terms and each argued the rights and wrongs of matters before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Jifu and Li Jiang were at odds and each argued his case before the throne.

sentences.zh: 元衡居中，無所違附，上稱為長者。

translations.literal: Yuanheng stood between them, siding with neither, and the emperor called him a man of mature judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng stood between them, favoring neither, and the emperor praised him as a man of mature judgment.

sentences.zh: 及吉甫卒，上方討淮、蔡，悉以機務委之。

translations.literal: When Jifu died, the emperor was then campaigning against Huai and Cai and entrusted all critical affairs to Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Jifu died, while the emperor was campaigning against Huai and Cai, he entrusted all critical affairs to Yuanheng.

sentences.zh: 時王承宗遣使奏事，請赦吳元濟。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Chengzong sent envoys to report affairs and to request an amnesty for Wu Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong then sent envoys to report affairs and to request an amnesty for Wu Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 請事於宰相，辭禮悖慢，元衡叱之。

translations.literal: When they came before the chief ministers their words and demeanor were insolent, and Yuanheng rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: When they appeared before the chief ministers their manner was insolent, and Yuanheng rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 承宗因飛章詆元衡，咎怨頗結。

translations.literal: Chengzong therefore sent a memorial slandering Yuanheng, and enmity between them grew deep.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong then sent a memorial defaming Yuanheng, and bitter resentment took root between them.

sentences.zh: 元衡宅在靜安裏，十年六月三日，將朝，出裏東門，有暗中叱使滅燭者，導騎訶之，賊射之，中肩。

translations.literal: Yuanheng's residence was in Jing'an Ward. On the third day of the sixth month of the tenth year, as he was going to court and left the east gate of the ward, someone in the dark shouted for the torches to be extinguished; his outriders reproved him, and the assassins shot Yuanheng in the shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng lived in Jing'an Ward. On the third day of the sixth month of year 10, as he set out for court and passed the ward's east gate, a voice in the dark ordered the torches put out; his outriders challenged the speaker, and assassins shot Yuanheng in the shoulder.

sentences.zh: 又有匿樹陰突出者，以棓擊元衡左股。

translations.literal: Another man hidden in the shade of a tree suddenly rushed out and struck Yuanheng on the left thigh with a club.
translations.idiomatic: Another man concealed in the shade of a tree rushed out and struck Yuanheng on the left thigh with a club.

sentences.zh: 其徒馭已為賊所格奔逸，賊乃持元衡馬，東南行十餘步害之，批其顱骨懷去。

translations.literal: His attendants and grooms had already been beaten off and fled; the assassins then seized Yuanheng's horse, dragged him southeast more than ten paces, and killed him, hacking away his skull and carrying it off.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants and grooms had already been beaten off and fled; the killers then seized Yuanheng's horse, dragged him more than ten paces to the southeast, and killed him, hacking off his skull and carrying it away.

sentences.zh: 及眾呼偕至，持火照之，見元衡已踣於血中，即元衡宅東北隅墻之外。

translations.literal: When the crowd cried out and gathered, they held up torches and saw Yuanheng already fallen in a pool of blood, just beyond the northeast corner wall of his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When others rushed up with torches they found Yuanheng fallen in blood just beyond the northeast corner of his compound wall.

sentences.zh: 時夜漏未盡，陌上多朝騎及行人，鋪卒連呼十餘里，皆云賊殺宰相，聲達朝堂，百官恟恟，未知死者誰也。

translations.literal: The night watches had not yet ended; on the streets were many court riders and passersby, and patrolmen called out for more than ten li—everyone saying the chief minister had been murdered; the cry reached the court hall and the officials were thrown into panic, not yet knowing who had died.
translations.idiomatic: The night watches had not yet ended; the streets were full of riders bound for court and pedestrians, and patrolmen raised the alarm for more than ten li—all crying that the chief minister had been slain. The clamor reached the palace and officials panicked, not yet knowing who had died.

sentences.zh: 須臾，元衡馬走至，遇人始辨之。

translations.literal: Before long Yuanheng's horse came running back, and only then did people recognize what had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuanheng's horse came galloping back, and only then did people realize what had happened.

sentences.zh: 既明，仗至紫宸門，有司以元衡遇害聞。

translations.literal: When day broke, the imperial guard reached the Gate of Purple Felicity, and the responsible officials reported that Yuanheng had been murdered.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the imperial guard reached the Gate of Purple Felicity, and the responsible officials reported Yuanheng's murder.

sentences.zh: 上震驚，卻朝而坐延英，召見宰相。

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken, canceled the morning audience, and sat in Yanying Hall, summoning the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shaken, canceled the morning audience, and sat in Yanying Hall to summon the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 惋慟者久之，為之再不食。

translations.literal: He grieved for a long time and twice refused food.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved at length and twice refused his meals.

sentences.zh: 冊贈司徒，贈賻布帛五百匹、粟四百碩，輟朝五日，謚曰忠湣。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was posthumously enfeoffed as grand mentor, granted five hundred bolts of cloth and silk and four hundred piculs of grain as funeral gifts, court mourning was suspended for five days, and his posthumous title was Loyal and Lamented.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as grand mentor, granted five hundred bolts of cloth and silk and four hundred piculs of grain as funeral gifts, court mourning was suspended for five days, and his posthumous title was Loyal and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 元衡工五言詩，好事者傳之，往往被於管弦。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was skilled at pentasyllabic verse; enthusiasts transmitted his poems, and they were often set to music.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng excelled at pentasyllabic poetry; admirers circulated his verses, and they were often set to music.

sentences.zh: 初，八年，元衡自蜀再輔政，時太白犯上相，歷執法。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the eighth year, when Yuanheng returned from Shu to serve again as chief minister, the planet Venus transgressed the asterism of the chief minister and the offices of law enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in year 8, when Yuanheng returned from Shu to serve again as chief minister, Venus transgressed the asterism of the chief minister and the offices of law enforcement.

sentences.zh: 占者言：「今之三相皆不利，始輕末重。

translations.literal: The diviners said, "The three chief ministers of the day are all ill-fated; the beginning is light and the end heavy."
translations.idiomatic: Diviners said, "All three chief ministers of the day are ill-fated; the beginning is light and the end heavy."

sentences.zh: 」月餘，李絳以足疾免。

translations.literal: More than a month later Li Jiang was dismissed because of illness in the foot.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later Li Jiang was dismissed because of a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，李吉甫以暴疾卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year Li Jifu died of a sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the following year Li Jifu died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 至是，元衡為盜所害，年五十八。

translations.literal: By then Yuanheng had been murdered by bandits; he was fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuanheng had been murdered by assassins; he was fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 始元衡與吉甫齊年，又同日為宰相。

translations.literal: From the first Yuanheng and Jifu were the same age and were appointed chief ministers on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset Yuanheng and Jifu were the same age and were appointed chief ministers on the same day.

sentences.zh: 及出鎮，分領揚、益。

translations.literal: When they went out to command regions, they respectively governed Yang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When they went out to command regions, one governed Yangzhou and the other Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 及吉甫再入，元衡亦還。

translations.literal: When Jifu returned to court, Yuanheng also came back.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu returned to the capital, Yuanheng also came back.

sentences.zh: 吉甫先一年以元衡生月卒，元衡後一年以吉甫生月卒。

translations.literal: Jifu died one year earlier, in the month of Yuanheng's birth; Yuanheng died one year later, in the month of Jifu's birth.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu died one year earlier in the month of Yuanheng's birth; Yuanheng died one year later in the month of Jifu's birth.

sentences.zh: 吉兇之數，若符會焉。

translations.literal: The numbers of fortune and misfortune seemed to match as if by design.
translations.idiomatic: The tallies of fortune and misfortune seemed to align as if by design.

sentences.zh: 先是，長安謠曰「打麥麥打三三三」，既而旋其袖曰「舞了也」。

translations.literal: Earlier a rhyme in Chang'an ran, "Thresh the wheat, wheat thresh three three three," and then, turning up the sleeve, "The dance is done."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a rhyme in Chang'an ran, "Thresh the wheat, wheat thresh three three three," and then, turning up the sleeve, "The dance is done."

sentences.zh: 解者謂：「打麥」者，打麥時也；

translations.literal: Interpreters said, "Thresh the wheat" means the time of threshing wheat;
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters said "thresh the wheat" meant the season of threshing wheat;

sentences.zh: 「麥打」者，蓋謂暗中突擊也；

translations.literal: "wheat thresh" meant a sudden strike from concealment;
translations.idiomatic: "wheat thresh" meant a sudden strike from hiding;

sentences.zh: 「三三三」，謂六月三日也；

translations.literal: "three three three" meant the third day of the sixth month;
translations.idiomatic: "three three three" meant the third day of the sixth month;

sentences.zh: 「舞了也」，謂元衡之卒也。

translations.literal: "the dance is done" meant Yuanheng's death.
translations.idiomatic: "the dance is done" meant Yuanheng's death.

sentences.zh: 自是京師大恐，城門加衛兵，察其出入，物色伺之。

translations.literal: From then on the capital was greatly alarmed; guards were added at the city gates to inspect those entering and leaving and to watch for suspects.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the capital was gripped by fear; guards were added at the gates to inspect those entering and leaving and to watch for suspects.

sentences.zh: 其偉狀異制、燕趙之音者，多執訊之。

translations.literal: Men of imposing stature, unusual dress, or Yan-Zhao accents were often seized and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Men of imposing build, unusual dress, or Yan-Zhao accents were often seized and interrogated.

sentences.zh: 元衡從父弟儒衡。

translations.literal: Yuanheng had a younger cousin on his father's side named Ruheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng had a younger cousin on his father's side named Ruheng.

sentences.zh: 儒衡，字庭碩。

translations.literal: Ruheng, courtesy name Tingshuo.
translations.idiomatic: Ruheng, whose courtesy name was Tingshuo.

sentences.zh: 才度俊偉，氣直貌莊，言不妄發，與人交友，終始不渝。

translations.literal: His talent and bearing were lofty and handsome; his spirit was upright and his appearance grave; he did not speak rashly, and in friendship he never wavered from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and imposing in bearing, upright in spirit and grave in appearance, he never spoke rashly and in friendship never wavered from first to last.

sentences.zh: 相國鄭余慶不事華潔，後進趨其門者多垢衣敗服，以望其知。

translations.literal: Chief minister Zheng Yuqing did not pursue lavish display, and many younger men who sought his favor came to his gate in soiled clothes and worn garments to win his notice.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zheng Yuqing shunned lavish display, and many younger men who sought his favor came to his gate in shabby dress to win his notice.

sentences.zh: 而儒衡謁見，未嘗輒易所好，但與之正言直論，余慶因亦重之。

translations.literal: Yet when Ruheng called on him he never casually changed his own habits, but spoke with him in plain, direct terms, and Yuqing therefore also respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Ruheng visited he never casually changed his own habits but spoke with Yuqing in plain, direct terms, and Yuqing therefore respected him as well.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以元衡橫死王事，嘗嗟惜之，故待儒衡甚厚。

translations.literal: Because Yuanheng had died violently in the service of the state, Xianzong had often sighed in regret, and therefore treated Ruheng with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuanheng had died violently in imperial service, Xianzong had often sighed in regret and therefore treated Ruheng with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十二年，權知諫議大夫事，尋兼知制誥。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was temporarily placed in charge of remonstrance affairs and soon concurrently given charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was temporarily placed in charge of remonstrance affairs and soon concurrently given charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 皇甫镈以宰相領度支，剝下以媚上，無敢言其罪者。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo, serving as chief minister while heading the treasury, stripped the people to please the throne, and no one dared speak of his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo, serving as chief minister while heading the treasury, stripped the people to please the throne, and no one dared accuse him.

sentences.zh: 儒衡上疏論列，镈密訴其事，帝曰：「勿以儒衡上疏，卿將報怨耶！

translations.literal: Ruheng submitted a memorial setting forth the abuses, and Bo secretly reported the matter; the emperor said, "Do not take Ruheng's memorial as grounds for you to settle a grudge!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruheng submitted a memorial setting forth the abuses; Bo secretly reported the matter, and the emperor said, "Do not treat Ruheng's memorial as grounds for you to settle a grudge!"

sentences.zh: 」镈不復敢言。

translations.literal: Bo did not dare speak further.
translations.idiomatic: Bo did not dare speak further.

sentences.zh: 儒衡氣岸高雅，論事有風彩，群邪惡之。

translations.literal: Ruheng's bearing was lofty and elegant, and when he discussed affairs he had distinction; the wicked hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Ruheng's bearing was lofty and elegant, and when he discussed affairs he had real distinction; the wicked hated him.

sentences.zh: 尤為宰相令狐楚所忌。

translations.literal: He was especially hated by chief minister Linghu Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially hated by chief minister Linghu Chu.

sentences.zh: 元和末年，垂將大用，楚畏其明俊，欲以計沮之，以離其寵。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Yuanhe reign, as he was about to receive major appointment, Chu feared his brilliance and sought by stratagem to obstruct him and alienate him from favor.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuanhe reign, as he was about to receive major appointment, Chu feared his brilliance and sought by stratagem to obstruct him and alienate him from favor.

sentences.zh: 有狄兼謨者，梁公仁傑之後，時為襄陽從事。

translations.literal: There was one Di Jianmo, a descendant of the Duke of Liang Di Renjie, who at the time served on the staff at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Di Jianmo, a descendant of the Duke of Liang Di Renjie, then serving on the staff at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 楚乃自草制詞，召狄兼謨為拾遺，曰：「朕聽政余暇，躬覽國書，知奸臣擅權之由，見母后竊位之事。

translations.literal: Chu himself drafted an edict and summoned Di Jianmo as remonstrance official, saying, "In my spare hours from hearing government I have myself perused the national records and learned how treacherous ministers seized power and how the empress dowager usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chu himself drafted an edict and summoned Di Jianmo as remonstrance official, saying, "In my spare hours from hearing government I have myself perused the national records and learned how treacherous ministers seized power and how the empress dowager usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 我國家神器大寶，將遂傳於他人。

translations.literal: The sacred vessel and great treasure of our state were about to be handed on to others.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred vessel and great treasure of our state were about to be handed on to others.

sentences.zh: 洪惟昊穹，降鑒儲祉，誕生仁傑，保佑中宗，使絕維更張，明辟乃復。

translations.literal: Solemnly did Heaven look down and send down stored blessing: Renjie was born to protect Zhongzong, so that the severed cord was retied and the enlightened ruler was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Solemnly did Heaven look down and send down stored blessing: Renjie was born to protect Zhongzong, so that the severed cord was retied and the enlightened ruler was restored.

sentences.zh: 宜福胄胤，與國無窮。

translations.literal: May his descendants be blessed and share the state without end."
translations.idiomatic: May his descendants be blessed and share the state without end."

sentences.zh: 」及兼謨制出，儒衡泣訴於御前，言其祖平一在天后朝辭榮終老，當時不以為累。

translations.literal: When Jianmo's draft was issued, Ruheng wept and appealed before the throne, saying that his grandfather Pingyi in the reign of the Empress Wu had declined honor and ended his days in retirement, and at the time was not regarded as a burden.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianmo's draft was issued, Ruheng wept and appealed before the throne, saying that his grandfather Pingyi in the reign of Empress Wu had declined honor and ended his days in retirement without being regarded as a burden on the family.

sentences.zh: 憲宗再三撫慰之。

translations.literal: Xianzong repeatedly comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong repeatedly comforted him.

sentences.zh: 自是薄楚之為人。

translations.literal: From then on he thought lightly of Chu's character.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on he held Chu in low esteem.

sentences.zh: 然儒衡守道不回，嫉惡太甚，終不至大任。

translations.literal: Yet Ruheng held to the Way without wavering, hated evil excessively, and in the end never reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ruheng held fast to principle without bending, detested wickedness too fiercely, and in the end never rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 尋正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was formally appointed drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon formally appointed drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時元稹依倚內官，得知制誥，儒衡深鄙之。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Zhen relied on inner eunuchs to gain charge of drafting edicts; Ruheng despised him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Zhen relied on palace eunuchs to win charge of drafting edicts, and Ruheng despised him deeply.

sentences.zh: 會食瓜閣下，蠅集於上，儒衡以扇揮之曰：「適從何處來，而遽集於此？

translations.literal: Once, while eating melon beneath a pavilion, flies gathered on it, and Ruheng waved them away with a fan, saying, "Where have you just come from that you hasten to gather here?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, while eating melon in a pavilion, flies gathered on it; Ruheng fanned them away and said, "Where have you just come from that you hasten to gather here?"

sentences.zh: 」同僚失色，儒衡意氣自若。

translations.literal: His colleagues turned pale, but Ruheng remained composed in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues turned pale, but Ruheng remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changqing he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing year 4 he died, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶，字居業，滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqing, courtesy name Juye, was a native of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing, whose courtesy name was Juye, came from Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 祖長裕，官至國子司業，終潁川太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Changyu reached the office of vice director of the Directorate of Education and ended as prefect of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Changyu rose to vice director of the Directorate of Education and ended his career as prefect of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 長裕弟少微，為中書舍人、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Changyu's younger brother Shaowei served as drafting secretary in the Secretariat and vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu's younger brother Shaowei served as drafting secretary in the Secretariat and vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 兄弟有名於當時。

translations.literal: The brothers were famous in their day.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were celebrated in their day.

sentences.zh: 父慈，與元德秀友善，官至太子舍人。

translations.literal: His father Ci was on friendly terms with Yuan Dexiu and reached the office of attendant of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ci was friendly with Yuan Dexiu and rose to serve as attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 餘慶少勤學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Yuqing was diligent in study from youth and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuqing studied diligently and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 大歷中舉進士。

translations.literal: In the Dali reign he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 建中末，山南節度使嚴震辟為從事，累官殿中侍御史，丁父憂罷。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianzhong reign Yan Zhen, military commissioner of Shannan, summoned him as staff member; he rose to attendant censor in the palace and resigned on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jianzhong, Yan Zhen, military commissioner of Shannan, took him onto his staff; he rose to palace attendant censor and left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 貞元初入朝，歷左司、兵部員外郎，庫部郎中。

translations.literal: When Zhenyuan began he entered court service and passed through left bureau director, supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of War, and director in the Ministry of Stores.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he entered court service, serving as left bureau director, supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of War, and director in the Ministry of Stores.

sentences.zh: 八年，選為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was selected as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was selected as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月，遷工部侍郎，知吏部選事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of works and given charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 13 he was promoted to vice minister of works and placed in charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 時有玄法寺僧法湊為寺眾所訴，萬年縣尉盧伯達斷還俗，後又復為僧，伯達上表論之。

translations.literal: At the time the monk Facou of Xuanshi Temple was sued by the monastic community; the Wannian county assistant Lu Boda ruled that he return to lay life, but later he became a monk again, and Boda submitted a memorial on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the monk Facou of Xuanshi Temple was sued by his monastic community; Wannian county assistant Lu Boda ruled that he return to lay life, but Facou became a monk again, and Boda submitted a memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 詔中丞宇文邈、刑部侍郎張彧、大理卿鄭雲逵等三司，與功德使判官諸葛述同按鞫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Yu Wen Yao, Vice Minister of Justice Zhang Yu, Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Zheng Yunkui, and others of the three offices, together with the administrative aide Zhuge Shu of the commissioner of merit, to investigate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Yu Wen Yao, Vice Minister of Justice Zhang Yu, Chief Judge Zheng Yunkui, and others of the three offices, together with administrative aide Zhuge Shu of the commissioner of merit, to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 時議述胥吏，不合與憲臣等同入省按事。

translations.literal: At the time opinion held that Shu was a petty clerk and unfit to enter the ministries together with censorial officials to conduct investigations.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that Shu was a petty clerk and unfit to enter the ministries with censorial officials to conduct investigations.

sentences.zh: 餘慶上疏論列，當時翕然稱重。

translations.literal: Yuqing submitted a memorial setting forth the abuses, and at the time all praised him together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing submitted a memorial setting forth the abuses, and the court praised him in unison.

sentences.zh: 十四年，拜中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 餘慶通究《六經》深旨，奏對之際，多以古義傅之。

translations.literal: Yuqing had thoroughly mastered the deep meaning of the Six Classics, and in memorials and responses he often applied ancient principles.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing had thoroughly mastered the deep meaning of the Six Classics and in memorials and responses often applied ancient principles.

sentences.zh: 與度支使於素善，每奏事餘慶皆議可之。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with the revenue commissioner Yu Su; whenever Yu memorialized, Yuqing would approve it.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with revenue commissioner Yu Su; whenever Yu memorialized, Yuqing would approve it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以罪貶。

translations.literal: Before long Yu was demoted for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu was demoted for a crime.

sentences.zh: 時又歲旱人饑，德宗與宰臣議，將賑給禁衛六軍。

translations.literal: At the time there was also drought and famine; Dezong discussed with the chief ministers plans to provide relief to the six armies of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the time drought and famine also afflicted the realm; Dezong discussed with the chief ministers plans to provide relief to the six armies of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 事未行，為中書吏所泄，餘慶貶郴州司馬，凡六載。

translations.literal: The matter had not yet been carried out when it was leaked by a clerk in the Secretariat; Yuqing was demoted to assistant prefect of Chenzhou, altogether six years.
translations.idiomatic: Before it could be carried out the plan was leaked by a Secretariat clerk; Yuqing was demoted to assistant prefect of Chenzhou for six years.

sentences.zh: 順宗登極，徵拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne, Yuqing was summoned and appointed left vice minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended the throne, Yuqing was summoned and appointed left vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗣位之月，又擢守本官、平章事。

translations.literal: In the month when Xianzong succeeded to the throne, he was again promoted to hold his original office and made chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the month Xianzong succeeded to the throne, Yuqing was again promoted to his former office and made chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，屬夏州將楊惠琳阻命，宰臣等論奏，多議兵事。

translations.literal: Before long the Xiazhou commander Yang Huilin defied orders; when the chief ministers discussed and memorialized, most spoke of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiazhou commander Yang Huilin defied orders; when the chief ministers discussed the matter, most spoke of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 餘慶復以古義上言，夏州軍士皆仰給縣官，又有「介馬萬蹄」之語。

translations.literal: Yuqing again spoke according to ancient principles, saying that the soldiers of Xiazhou all depended on the state for provisions, and citing the phrase "ten thousand hooves of relay horses."
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing again spoke from ancient precedent, noting that Xiazhou soldiers all depended on the state for provisions and citing the phrase "ten thousand hooves of relay horses."

sentences.zh: 時議以餘慶雖好古博雅而未適時。

translations.literal: At the time opinion held that although Yuqing loved antiquity and was broadly learned, he was not suited to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that although Yuqing loved antiquity and was broadly learned, he was ill suited to the times.

sentences.zh: 有主書滑渙，久司中書簿籍，與內官典樞密劉光琦情通。

translations.literal: There was a chief clerk Hua Huan who for a long time managed the Secretariat registers and was intimate with the eunuch Liu Guangqi, who controlled confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: There was chief clerk Hua Huan, who for years managed Secretariat registers and was intimate with eunuch Liu Guangqi, who controlled confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 宰相議事，與光琦異同者，令渙達意，未嘗不遂所欲。

translations.literal: When chief ministers discussed affairs, if their views differed from Guangqi's, Huan would convey Guangqi's intent, and their wishes were never denied.
translations.idiomatic: When chief ministers discussed affairs, if their views differed from Guangqi's, Huan would convey Guangqi's intent, and their wishes were never denied.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜佑、鄭絪皆姑息之。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Du You and Zheng Yin both indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Du You and Zheng Yin both indulged him.

sentences.zh: 議者雲佑私呼為滑八，四方書幣貲貨，充集其門，弟泳官至刺史。

translations.literal: Critics said You privately called him "Hua Eight"; gifts and valuables from all quarters filled his gate, and his younger brother Yong reached the office of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said You privately called him "Hua Eight"; gifts from all quarters filled his gate, and his younger brother Yong rose to prefect.

sentences.zh: 及餘慶再入中書，與同僚集議。

translations.literal: When Yuqing again entered the Secretariat, he met with colleagues to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqing again entered the Secretariat, he met with colleagues to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 渙指陳是非，餘慶怒其僭，叱之。

translations.literal: Huan pointed out rights and wrongs; Yuqing was angry at his presumption and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan pointed out rights and wrongs; Yuqing, angered by his presumption, rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 尋而餘慶罷相，為太子賓客。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yuqing was removed as chief minister and made guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuqing was removed as chief minister and made guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，渙贓汙發，賜死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year Huan's corruption was exposed and he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year Huan's corruption was exposed and he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 上浸聞餘慶叱渙事，甚重之，乃改為國子祭酒，尋拜河南尹。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually heard of Yuqing's rebuke of Huan and greatly respected him; he was therefore changed to grand director of the Directorate of Education and soon appointed metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gradually heard of Yuqing's rebuke of Huan and greatly respected him; he was therefore made grand director of the Directorate of Education and soon appointed metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 三年，檢校兵部尚書，兼東都留守。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed acting minister of war and concurrently eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was appointed acting minister of war and concurrently eastern capital regent.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，正拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year he was formally appointed minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 6 he was formally appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 餘慶再為相，罷免皆非大過，尤以清儉為時所稱。

translations.literal: Yuqing twice served as chief minister; his dismissals were never for grave faults, and he was especially praised in his time for purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing twice served as chief minister; his dismissals were never for grave faults, and he was especially praised for purity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 洎中外踐更，郁為耆德，朝廷得失，言成準的。

translations.literal: As men within and outside the court rose and fell in office, he became an elder statesman, and his words on the court's gains and losses became the standard.
translations.idiomatic: As men within and outside the court rose and fell, he became an elder statesman whose words on the court's gains and losses set the standard.

sentences.zh: 時京兆尹元義方、戶部侍郎判度支盧坦，皆以勛官前任至三品，據令合立門戟，各請戟立於其第。

translations.literal: At the time Metropolitan Governor Yuan Yifang and Vice Minister of Revenue Lu Tan, who concurrently headed the treasury, were both meritorious officials whose previous posts had reached third rank; according to regulations they were entitled to set up halberds at their gates, and each requested halberds at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Metropolitan Governor Yuan Yifang and Vice Minister of Revenue Lu Tan, who headed the treasury, were meritorious officials whose previous posts had reached third rank; by regulation they were entitled to halberds at their gates, and each requested them.

sentences.zh: 時義方以加上柱國、坦以前任宣州觀察使請戟。

translations.literal: Yifang relied on his honorary title of pillar of state; Tan relied on his former post as military commissioner of Xuanzhou in requesting halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang relied on his honorary title of pillar of state; Tan relied on his former post as military commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 近代立戟者，率有銀青階，而義方只據勛官，有司不詳覆而給之，議者非之，臺司將劾而未果。

translations.literal: In recent times those who set up halberds generally also held silver-and-cyan rank, but Yifang relied only on meritorious rank; the responsible office did not examine the matter carefully and granted it; critics disapproved, and the censorate was about to impeach but did not carry it through.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times those who set up halberds generally also held silver-and-cyan rank, but Yifang relied only on meritorious rank; the responsible office granted halberds without careful review; critics disapproved, and the censorate was about to impeach but did not follow through.

sentences.zh: 會餘慶自東都來，發論大以為不可。

translations.literal: When Yuqing came from the eastern capital, he spoke out strongly that this could not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqing came from the eastern capital, he spoke out strongly that this could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 由是，臺司移牒詰禮部，左司郎中陸則、禮部員外崔備皆罰俸，奪元、盧之門戟。

translations.literal: Thereupon the censorate sent a dispatch questioning the Ministry of Rites; Left Bureau Director Lu Ze and Supernumerary Clerk in the Ministry of Rites Cui Bei were both fined salary, and Yuan and Lu had their gate halberds taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the censorate sent a dispatch questioning the Ministry of Rites; Left Bureau Director Lu Ze and Supernumerary Clerk Cui Bei were both fined salary, and Yuan and Lu had their gate halberds removed.

sentences.zh: 餘慶受詔撰《惠昭太子哀冊》，其辭甚工。

translations.literal: Yuqing received an edict to compose the Lament for the Heir Apparent Huizhao; the text was very accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing received an edict to compose the Lament for the Heir Apparent Huizhao; the text was highly accomplished.

sentences.zh: 有醫工崔環，自淮南小將為黃州司馬。

translations.literal: There was a medical artisan Cui Huan who rose from a minor officer in Huainan to assistant prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was medical artisan Cui Huan, who rose from a minor officer in Huainan to assistant prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敕至南省，餘慶執之封還，以為諸道散將無故授正員五品官，是開僥幸之路，且無闕可供。

translations.literal: When the edict reached the Secretariat, Yuqing held it and returned it sealed, holding that for scattered officers of the circuits to be appointed without cause to regular fifth-rank posts opened a path of improper favor and there were no vacancies to fill.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached the Secretariat, Yuqing held it and returned it sealed, arguing that appointing scattered circuit officers without cause to regular fifth-rank posts opened a path of improper favor and there were no vacancies to fill.

sentences.zh: 言或過理，由是稍忤時權，改太子少傅，兼判太常卿事。

translations.literal: His words sometimes exceeded reason, and for this he gradually offended those in power; he was changed to junior guardian of the heir apparent and concurrently given charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His words sometimes exceeded reason, and for this he gradually offended those in power; he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent and concurrently given charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 初德宗自山南還宮，關輔有懷光、吐蕃之虞，都下驚憂，遂詔太常集樂去大鼓。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Dezong returned from Shannan to the palace, there were fears of Huai Guang and the Tibetans in the capital region; the capital was alarmed, and an edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to assemble music but remove the great drums.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Dezong returned from Shannan, there were fears of Huai Guang and the Tibetans in the capital region; the capital was alarmed, and an edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to assemble music but remove the great drums.

sentences.zh: 至是，餘慶始奏復用大鼓。

translations.literal: By now Yuqing memorialized to restore the use of great drums.
translations.idiomatic: By now Yuqing memorialized to restore the use of great drums.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜檢校右僕射，兼興元尹，充山南西道節度觀察使，三歲受代。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed acting right vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently metropolitan governor of Xingyuan, and military commissioner and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit; after three years he was replaced.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was appointed acting right vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently metropolitan governor of Xingyuan, and military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit; after three years he was replaced.

sentences.zh: 十二年，除太子少師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed junior preceptor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was appointed junior preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋以年及懸車，請致仕，詔不許。

translations.literal: Soon, having reached the age for suspending the carriage, he requested retirement, but the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, having reached the age for retirement, he requested to withdraw, but the throne did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 時累有恩赦敘階，及天子親謁郊廟，行事官等皆得以恩授三品五品，不復計考，其使府賓吏，又以軍功借賜命服而後入拜者十八九。

translations.literal: At the time there were repeated amnesties restoring ranks, and when the Son of Heaven personally visited the suburban altars, officiating officials could all receive third- or fifth-rank grants by favor without regard to examination; staff members and clerks of commissioners' offices also borrowed military merit to obtain court robes before entering audience—eight or nine out of ten did so.
translations.idiomatic: At the time repeated amnesties restored ranks, and when the Son of Heaven personally visited the suburban altars, officiating officials could receive third- or fifth-rank grants by favor without examination; commissioners' staff also borrowed military merit to obtain court robes before audience—eight or nine in ten did so.

sentences.zh: 由是，在朝衣綠者甚少，郎官諫官有被紫垂金者。

translations.literal: Therefore few at court still wore green; remonstrance officials and bureau directors sometimes wore purple with gold ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore few at court still wore green; remonstrance officials and bureau directors sometimes wore purple with gold ornaments.

sentences.zh: 又丞郎中謝洎郎官出使，多賜章服，以示加恩。

translations.literal: Moreover, when vice directors and directors went out on mission, they were often granted patterned robes to show added favor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when vice directors and directors went out on mission, they were often granted patterned robes to show added favor.

sentences.zh: 於是寵章尤濫，當時不以服章為貴，遂詔餘慶詳格令，立制條，奏以聞。

translations.literal: Thus insignia became especially excessive; at the time patterned robes were no longer prized, and an edict ordered Yuqing to examine the regulations in detail, establish rules, and memorialize for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Thus insignia became especially excessive; patterned robes were no longer prized, and an edict ordered Yuqing to examine the regulations, establish rules, and memorialize for approval.

sentences.zh: 十三年，拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed left vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was appointed left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自兵興以來，處左右端揆之位者多非其人，及餘慶以名臣居之，人情美洽。

translations.literal: Since military troubles began, many who held the left and right chief minister posts were unfit; when Yuqing, a renowned minister, occupied the post, public sentiment was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Since military troubles began, many who held the chief minister posts were unfit; when Yuqing, a renowned minister, occupied the post, public sentiment was pleased.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以餘慶諳練典章，朝廷禮樂制度有乖故事，專委餘慶參酌施行，遂用為詳定使。

translations.literal: Because Yuqing was versed in canonical regulations and court ritual and music systems often diverged from precedent, Xianzong specially entrusted Yuqing to consult and implement them, and therefore used him as commissioner of detailed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuqing was versed in canonical regulations and court ritual often diverged from precedent, Xianzong entrusted him to consult and implement them and appointed him commissioner of detailed regulations.

sentences.zh: 余慶復奏刑部侍郎韓愈、禮部侍郎李程為副使，左司郎中崔郾、吏部郎中陳珮、刑部員外郎楊嗣復、禮部員外郎庾敬休，並充詳定判官。

translations.literal: Yuqing memorialized again that Vice Minister of Justice Han Yu and Vice Minister of Rites Li Cheng serve as deputy commissioners, and Left Bureau Director Cui Yan, Director in the Ministry of Personnel Chen Pei, Supernumerary Clerk in the Ministry of Justice Yang Sifu, and Supernumerary Clerk in the Ministry of Rites Yu Jingxiu all serve as detailed-regulation administrative judges.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing memorialized that Vice Minister of Justice Han Yu and Vice Minister of Rites Li Cheng serve as deputy commissioners, with Cui Yan, Chen Pei, Yang Sifu, and Yu Jingxiu as administrative judges.

sentences.zh: 朝廷儀制、吉兇五禮，鹹有損益焉。

translations.literal: Court ceremonial systems and the five rites of fortune and misfortune all had additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Court ceremonial systems and the five rites of fortune and misfortune all underwent revision.

sentences.zh: 改鳳翔尹、鳳翔隴節度使。

translations.literal: He was changed to metropolitan governor of Fengxiang and military commissioner of Fengxiang Long Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to metropolitan governor of Fengxiang and military commissioner of Fengxiang Long Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十四年，兼太子少師、檢校司空，封滎陽郡公，兼判國子祭酒事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was concurrently junior preceptor of the heir apparent, acting minister of works, enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang, and concurrently given charge of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was concurrently junior preceptor of the heir apparent, acting minister of works, enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang, and concurrently given charge of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 以太學荒毀日久，生徒不振，奏率文官俸給修兩京國子監。

translations.literal: Because the Imperial Academy had long lain in ruins and students were inactive, he memorialized that civil officials' salaries be drawn on to repair the Directorate of Education in the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Imperial Academy had long lain in ruins and students were inactive, he memorialized that civil officials' salaries be used to repair the Directorate of Education in the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 及穆宗登極，以師傅之舊，進位檢校司徒，優禮甚至。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, because of his old ties as tutor, Yuqing was promoted to acting minister of works with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended the throne, because of his old ties as tutor, Yuqing was promoted to acting minister of works with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年十一月卒，詔曰：「故金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒、兼太子少師、上柱國、滎陽郡開國公、食邑二千戶鄭餘慶，始以衣冠禮樂，行於山東，餘力文章，遂成誌學。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe the edict read: "The late Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Acting Minister of Works, Concurrently Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Pillar of State, Duke of Xingyang with a fief of two thousand households, Zheng Yuqing—he first carried ritual and music through Shandong; with his remaining strength in letters he completed his scholarly resolve."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yuanhe 15 the edict read: "The late Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Acting Minister of Works, Concurrently Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Pillar of State, Duke of Xingyang with a fief of two thousand households, Zheng Yuqing—he first carried ritual and music through Shandong; with his remaining strength in letters he completed his scholarly resolve."

sentences.zh: 出入清近，盈五十年。

translations.literal: He moved in and out of close imperial service for fully fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: He moved in and out of close imperial service for fully fifty years.

sentences.zh: 再秉臺衡，屢分戎律。

translations.literal: Twice he held the scales of government; repeatedly he shared in military command.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he held the scales of government; repeatedly he shared in military command.

sentences.zh: 凡所要職，無不踐更。

translations.literal: Every important office he held without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Every important office in turn he held without exception.

sentences.zh: 貴而能貧，卑以自牧。

translations.literal: Noble yet able to be poor, humble yet self-restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Noble yet able to live poor, humble yet self-restrained.

sentences.zh: 謇諤聞於臺閣，柔睦化於閨門。

translations.literal: His forthright remonstrance was heard in the censorate; gentleness and harmony transformed his household.
translations.idiomatic: His forthright remonstrance was heard at court; gentleness and harmony transformed his household.

sentences.zh: 受命有考父之恭，待士比公孫之廣。

translations.literal: In receiving orders he had the reverence of Kaofu; in treating scholars he had the breadth of Gongsun.
translations.idiomatic: In receiving orders he had the reverence of Kaofu; in treating scholars he had the breadth of Gongsun.

sentences.zh: 焚書逸禮，盡可口傳；

translations.literal: Burned books and lost rites he could all transmit by word of mouth;
translations.idiomatic: Burned books and lost rites he could transmit by word of mouth;

sentences.zh: 古史舊章，如因心匠。

translations.literal: ancient histories and old regulations he handled as if by the mind's craft.
translations.idiomatic: ancient histories and old regulations he handled as if shaped by the mind alone.

sentences.zh: 朕方咨稟，庶罔昏逾。

translations.literal: I was just consulting him, hoping to avoid confusion and error.
translations.idiomatic: I was just consulting him, hoping to avoid confusion and error.

sentences.zh: 神將祝予，痛悼何及！

translations.literal: The spirits will aid me—how can grief reach its limit!
translations.idiomatic: The spirits will aid me—how can grief reach its limit!

sentences.zh: 乞言既阻，赗禮宜優，可贈太保。

translations.literal: His counsel is now blocked; funeral gifts should be generous—he may be posthumously awarded Grand Mentor."
translations.idiomatic: His counsel is now blocked; funeral gifts should be generous—he may be posthumously awarded Grand Mentor."

sentences.zh: 」時年七十五，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He was then seventy-five; his posthumous title was Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was then seventy-five; his posthumous title was Upright.

sentences.zh: 餘慶砥名礪行，不失儒者之道；

translations.literal: Yuqing polished his name and honed his conduct, never departing from the way of the ru;
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing polished his name and honed his conduct, never departing from the way of the scholar;

sentences.zh: 清儉率素，終始不渝。

translations.literal: pure and frugal in plain simplicity, from first to last without change.
translations.idiomatic: pure and frugal in plain simplicity, from first to last without change.

sentences.zh: 四朝居將相之任，出入垂五十年，祿賜所得，分給親黨，其家頗類寒素。

translations.literal: Across four reigns he held the posts of general and chief minister, moving in and out for nearly fifty years; what he received in salary and gifts he distributed to kin, and his household resembled that of the poor and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Across four reigns he held the posts of general and chief minister for nearly fifty years; salary and gifts he distributed to kin, and his household resembled that of the poor and plain.

sentences.zh: 自至德已來，方鎮除授，必遣中使領旌節就第宣賜，皆厚以金帛遣之。

translations.literal: Since the Zhide reign, when frontier commanders were appointed and dismissed, the court always sent a palace envoy bearing insignia of office to their residences to proclaim the appointment, all richly rewarded with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhide reign, when frontier commanders were appointed, the court always sent a palace envoy bearing insignia to their residences to proclaim the appointment, richly rewarded with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 求媚者唯恐其數不廣，故王人一來，有獲錢數百萬者。

translations.literal: Those who sought favor feared the sum was not large enough, so a single envoy's visit could bring several million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought favor feared the sum was not large enough; a single envoy's visit could bring several million in cash.

sentences.zh: 餘慶每受方任，天子必誡其使曰：「餘慶家貧，不得妄有求取。

translations.literal: Whenever Yuqing received a regional appointment, the Son of Heaven would warn the envoy: "Yuqing's household is poor; you must not presume to seek anything from him."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yuqing received a regional appointment, the Son of Heaven would warn the envoy: "Yuqing's household is poor; you must not presume to seek anything from him."

sentences.zh: 」專欲振起儒教，後生謁見者，率以經學諷之。

translations.literal: He was bent on reviving Confucian teaching; younger men who called on him were generally admonished with classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was bent on reviving Confucian teaching; younger men who called on him were generally admonished with classical learning.

sentences.zh: 而周其所急，理家理身，極其儉薄。

translations.literal: Yet he attended to their urgent needs; in managing household and person he was extremely sparing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he attended to their urgent needs; in managing household and person he was extremely sparing.

sentences.zh: 及修官政，則喜開廣。

translations.literal: When administering official affairs he delighted in openness and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: When administering official affairs he delighted in openness and breadth.

sentences.zh: 鎮岐下一歲，戎事可觀。

translations.literal: Governing below Qi for one year, military affairs were commendable.
translations.idiomatic: Governing Fengxiang for one year, military affairs were commendable.

sentences.zh: 又創立儒宮以來，學者雖行己可學，而往往近於沽激，故當時議者不全德許之。

translations.literal: Since he founded the Confucian academy, although scholars could model themselves on his conduct, they often approached empty moral display; therefore critics of the day did not fully approve his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Since he founded the Confucian academy, although scholars could model his conduct, they often approached empty moral display; therefore critics did not fully approve his virtue.

sentences.zh: 上以家素清貧，不辦喪事，宜令所司特給一月俸料，以充賻贈，用示哀榮。

translations.literal: Because his household had long been poor and could not afford funeral arrangements, the responsible offices were specially ordered to grant one month's salary as funeral gifts to show mourning and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Because his household had long been poor and could not afford funeral arrangements, the responsible offices were ordered to grant one month's salary as funeral gifts to show mourning and honor.

sentences.zh: 有文集、表疏、碑誌、詩賦共五十卷行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings, memorials, inscriptions, dirges, and poetry in all totaled fifty juan circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings, memorials, inscriptions, dirges, and poetry totaling fifty juan circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 兄承慶，官不顯。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chengqing did not attain prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chengqing did not attain prominent office.

sentences.zh: 弟膺甫，官至主客員外郎中、楚懷鄭三州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yingfu reached supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Rites and director, and prefect of Chu, Huai, and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yingfu rose to supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Rites and served as prefect of Chu, Huai, and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 次弟具瞻、羽客、時然，皆官至縣令賓佐。

translations.literal: His next younger brothers Juzhan, Yuke, and Shiran all reached the offices of county magistrate or staff aide.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Juzhan, Yuke, and Shiran all rose to county magistrate or staff aide.

sentences.zh: 餘慶子澣。

translations.literal: Yuqing's son was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's son was Huan.

sentences.zh: 澣本名涵，以文宗籓邸時名同，改名澣。

translations.literal: Huan's original name was Han; because it was the same as the name of the princely establishment when Wenzong was heir, he was renamed Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's original name was Han; because it matched Wenzong's name when he was heir apparent, he was renamed Huan.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年舉進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 10 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 以父謫官，累年不任。

translations.literal: Because his father had been demoted, for many years he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had been demoted, he held no office for many years.

sentences.zh: 自秘書省校書郎遷洛陽尉，充集賢院修撰。

translations.literal: From collator in the Secretariat he was promoted to assistant in Luoyang and appointed compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: From collator in the Secretariat he became Luoyang assistant and compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 改長安尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: He was changed to assistant in Chang'an and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He became Chang'an assistant and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 轉太常寺主簿，職仍故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to registrar in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, his duties remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to registrar in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，改右補闕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and changed to right remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made right remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 獻疏切直，人為危之。

translations.literal: His submitted memorial was incisive and direct; people feared for his safety.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was incisive and direct; people feared for his safety.

sentences.zh: 及餘慶入朝，憲宗謂餘慶曰：「卿之令子，朕之直臣，可更相賀。

translations.literal: When Yuqing entered court, Xianzong said to Yuqing, "Your worthy son is my upright minister—you may congratulate each other."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqing entered court, Xianzong told him, "Your worthy son is my upright minister—you may congratulate each other."

sentences.zh: 」遂遷起居舍人，改考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was therefore promoted to recorder of the emperor's actions and changed to supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore promoted to recorder of the emperor's actions and made supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 刺史有驅迫人吏上言政績，請刊石紀政者，瀚探得其情，條責廉使，巧跡遂露，人服其敏識。

translations.literal: When a prefect drove and compelled clerks to memorialize his achievements and requested that his governance be carved in stone, Huan investigated and obtained the facts, set forth charges to the integrity commissioner, and the crafty traces were exposed; people admired his keen discernment.
translations.idiomatic: When a prefect drove clerks to memorialize his achievements and sought to have his governance carved in stone, Huan investigated, exposed the fraud to the integrity commissioner, and won admiration for his keen discernment.

sentences.zh: 時餘慶為僕射，請改省郎。

translations.literal: At the time Yuqing was vice director of the Secretariat and requested that his son be changed to another bureau post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuqing was vice director of the Secretariat and asked that his son be transferred to another bureau post.

sentences.zh: 乃換國子博士、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was therefore exchanged for erudite in the Directorate of Education and compiler at the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was exchanged for erudite in the Directorate of Education and compiler at the History Office.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，除喪，拜考功郎中。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when mourning ended he was appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 復丁內艱，終制，退居汜上。

translations.literal: He again mourned an inner relative; when mourning ended he retired to live on the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned again; when mourning ended he retired to the Si River region.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，征為司封郎中、史館修撰，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Changqing reign he was summoned as director in the Ministry of Revenue and compiler at the History Office, and was repeatedly promoted to drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing he was summoned as director in the Ministry of Revenue and History Office compiler, and rose to drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文宗登極，擢為翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Huan was promoted to Hanlin attendant and lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Huan was promoted to Hanlin attendant and lecturer.

sentences.zh: 上命撰《經史要錄》二十卷。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to compile the Essential Records of the Classics and Histories in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to compile the Essential Records of the Classics and Histories in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 書成，上喜其精博，因摘所上書語類。

translations.literal: When the book was completed the emperor was pleased with its breadth and precision and therefore selected categories from the language of memorials Huan had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was completed the emperor was pleased with its breadth and precision and drew categories from Huan's own memorial language.

sentences.zh: 上親自發問，瀚應對無滯，錫以金紫。

translations.literal: The emperor personally questioned him; Huan answered without hesitation and was granted the gold-and-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him in person; Huan answered without hesitation and was granted the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he was promoted to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 2 he was promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 典貢舉二年，選拔造秀，時號得人。

translations.literal: For two years he presided over the examinations and selected outstanding talent; at the time he was praised for finding the right men.
translations.idiomatic: For two years he presided over the examinations and selected outstanding talent; at the time he was praised for finding the right men.

sentences.zh: 轉兵部侍郎，改吏部，出為河南尹，皆著能名。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of war, changed to the Ministry of Personnel, and sent out as metropolitan governor of Henan—all with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of war, then personnel, then metropolitan governor of Henan—each post won him a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 入為左丞，旋拜刑部尚書，兼判左丞事。

translations.literal: He entered court as left vice director and soon was appointed minister of justice, concurrently given charge of left vice director affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as left vice director, soon became minister of justice, and concurrently handled left vice director affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為山南西道節度觀察使，檢校戶部尚書、興元尹、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was sent out as military commissioner and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, acting minister of revenue, metropolitan governor of Xingyuan, and concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, acting minister of revenue, metropolitan governor of Xingyuan, and concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 餘慶之鎮興元，創立儒宮，開設學館，至澣之來，復繼前美。

translations.literal: When Yuqing governed Xingyuan he founded a Confucian academy and opened study halls; when Huan came he continued the former excellence.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqing governed Xingyuan he founded a Confucian academy; when Huan came he continued that work.

sentences.zh: 開成四年閏正月，以戶部尚書徵。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the fourth year of Kaicheng he was summoned as minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of Kaicheng year 4 he was summoned as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 詔下之日，卒於興元，年六十四，贈右僕射，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: On the day the edict was issued he died at Xingyuan, aged sixty-four; he was posthumously awarded right vice director of the Secretariat and given the posthumous title Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the edict was issued he died at Xingyuan, aged sixty-four; he was posthumously made right vice director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 有文集、制誥共三十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings and drafted edicts totaled thirty juan and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings and drafted edicts totaling thirty juan circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 澣四子：允謨、茂諶、處誨、從讜。

translations.literal: Huan had four sons: Yunmo, Maochen, Chuhui, and Congzan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had four sons: Yunmo, Maochen, Chuhui, and Congzan.

sentences.zh: 允謨，以廕累官臺省，歷蜀、彭、濠、晉四州刺史，位終太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Yunmo, through yin privilege, accumulated offices in the censorate, served as prefect of Shu, Peng, Hao, and Jin, and ended as right guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yunmo, through yin privilege, rose in the censorate, served as prefect of Shu, Peng, Hao, and Jin, and ended as right guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 茂諶，避國諱改茂休，開成二年登進士第，四遷太常博士、兵部員外郎、吏部郎中、絳州刺史，位終秘書監。

translations.literal: Maochen, to avoid the dynastic taboo, changed his name to Maoxiu; in the second year of Kaicheng he passed the jinshi examination, was promoted four times to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of War, director in the Ministry of Personnel, and prefect of Jiang, and ended as director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Maochen, avoiding the dynastic taboo, changed his name to Maoxiu; in Kaicheng year 2 he passed the jinshi examination, rose through four promotions to erudite, war and personnel posts, and prefect of Jiang, and ended as director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 處誨，字延美，於昆仲間文章拔秀，早為士友所推。

translations.literal: Chuhui, courtesy name Yanmei, among his brothers stood out in letters and was early pushed by scholar-friends.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhui, whose courtesy name was Yanmei, stood out among his brothers in letters and was early esteemed by scholar-friends.

sentences.zh: 太和八年登進士第。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taihe he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 8 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 釋褐秘府，轉監察、拾遺、尚書郎、給事中。

translations.literal: On leaving the purple gate he served in the Secretariat, then investigating censor, remonstrance official, bureau director, and drafting reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving office he served in the Secretariat, then as investigating censor, remonstrance official, bureau director, and drafting reviewer.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部、刑部侍郎，出為越州刺史、浙東觀察使、檢校刑部尚書、汴州刺史、宣武軍節度觀察等使，卒於汴。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of works and justice, sent out as prefect of Yue and observation commissioner of Zhedong, acting minister of justice, prefect of Bian, and military commissioner of Xuanwu, and died at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of works and justice, served as prefect of Yue and Zhedong commissioner, acting minister of justice, and Xuanwu military commissioner, and died at Bian.

sentences.zh: 處誨族父朗。

translations.literal: Chuhui's clansman on his father's side was Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhui's paternal clansman was Lang.

sentences.zh: 初朗為定州節度使時，處誨為工部侍郎，因早朝假寐於待漏院，忽夢己為浙東觀察使，經過汴州，而朗為汴帥，留連飲餞，仰視屋棟，飾以黃土，賓從皆所識。

translations.literal: When Lang was military commissioner of Dingzhou and Chuhui was vice minister of works, during early court Chuhui dozed in the courtiers' waiting hall and suddenly dreamed he was observation commissioner of Zhedong; passing Bian, Lang was military commissioner of Bian and detained him for a farewell feast; looking up at the roof beams, they were decorated with yellow earth, and guests and attendants were all people he knew.
