translations.idiomatic: When Lang was military commissioner of Dingzhou and Chuhui was vice minister of works, during early court Chuhui dozed in the waiting hall and dreamed he was Zhedong commissioner; passing Bian he found Lang as Bian commissioner, who feasted him; the roof beams were decorated with yellow earth and all guests were familiar faces.

sentences.zh: 明年，朗果自定州鎮宣武，辟韋重掌書記。

translations.literal: The next year Lang indeed moved from Dingzhou to govern Xuanwu and summoned Wei Chong as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Lang moved from Dingzhou to govern Xuanwu and summoned Wei Chong as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 重將行，處誨告以所夢。

translations.literal: When Chong was about to depart, Chuhui told him of the dream.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong was about to depart, Chuhui told him of the dream.

sentences.zh: 明年，處誨轉刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year Chuhui was transferred to vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Chuhui was transferred to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，授浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed observation commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed observation commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 行及潼關，朗遣從事迎勞，仍致手書，令先疏所夢。

translations.literal: Reaching Tong Pass, Lang sent staff to welcome and comfort him and also sent a personal letter asking him first to write out the dream in detail.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass, Lang sent staff to welcome him and a personal letter asking him to write out the dream first.

sentences.zh: 比至汴，宴於清暑亭，賓佐悉符夢中。

translations.literal: When he reached Bian they feasted at the Pavilion of Clear Summer; guests and aides all matched the dream.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian they feasted at the Pavilion of Clear Summer; guests and aides all matched the dream.

sentences.zh: 朗仰視屋棟曰：「此亦黃土也。

translations.literal: Lang looked up at the roof beams and said, "This too is yellow earth."
translations.idiomatic: Lang looked up at the roof beams and said, "This too is yellow earth."

sentences.zh: 」四座感嘆移時。

translations.literal: The whole company sighed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The whole company sighed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 後五年，朗卒，處誨繼為汴州節度使，乃賦詩一章，刻於廳事，以盡思朗之悲。

translations.literal: Five years later Lang died; Chuhui succeeded him as military commissioner of Bianzhou and composed a poem, carving it in the hall office, to express fully his grief for Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later Lang died; Chuhui succeeded him as Bianzhou military commissioner and carved a poem in the hall to express his grief for Lang.

sentences.zh: 處誨方雅好古，且勤於著述，撰集至多。

translations.literal: Chuhui was refined, loved antiquity, and was diligent in writing; his compilations were extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhui was refined, loved antiquity, and wrote diligently; his compilations were extremely numerous.

sentences.zh: 為校書郎時，撰次《明皇雜錄》三篇，行於世。

translations.literal: When he was collator he compiled the Miscellaneous Records of Emperor Ming in three sections, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: As collator he compiled the Miscellaneous Records of Emperor Ming in three sections, which circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 從讜，字正求，會昌二年登進士第，釋褐秘書省校書郎，歷拾遺、補闕、尚書郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Congzan, courtesy name Zhengqiu, in the second year of Huichang passed the jinshi examination, left the purple gate as collator in the Secretariat, and passed through remonstrance official, suppletive remonstrance official, bureau director, and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan, whose courtesy name was Zhengqiu, passed the jinshi in Huichang year 2, served as Secretariat collator, and rose through remonstrance posts, bureau director, and edict drafter.

sentences.zh: 故相令狐綯、魏扶，皆父貢舉門生，為之延譽，尋遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Former chief ministers Linghu Tao and Wei Fu were both his father's examination protégés and extended reputation for him; soon he was promoted to drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Former chief ministers Linghu Tao and Wei Fu had been his father's examination protégés and praised him; he soon rose to drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 咸通三年，知貢舉，拜禮部侍郎，轉刑部，改吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiantong he presided over the examinations, was appointed vice minister of rites, transferred to justice, and changed to vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong year 3 he presided over examinations, became vice minister of rites, then justice, then personnel.

sentences.zh: 典選平允，時無屈人。

translations.literal: His conduct of selection was fair and even; at the time no one was wronged.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct of selection was fair; at the time no one was wronged.

sentences.zh: 垂將作輔，以權臣請托不行，改檢校刑部尚書、太原尹、北都留守、河東節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: About to become chief minister, because powerful ministers' requests were not granted he was changed to acting minister of justice, metropolitan governor of Taiyuan, northern capital regent, and military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: About to become chief minister, he refused powerful ministers' requests and was sent out as acting minister of justice, Taiyuan governor, northern capital regent, and Hedong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 逾年，乞還，不允，改檢校兵部尚書、汴州刺史、宣武軍節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he begged to return; permission was denied, and he was changed to acting minister of war, prefect of Bian, and military commissioner of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he begged to return; when refused he was made acting minister of war, Bian prefect, and Xuanwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 期年報政，美聲流聞。

translations.literal: Within a year he reported achievements in governance and fine reputation spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year his governance won praise and his reputation spread.

sentences.zh: 當途者懼其大用，改廣州刺史、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Those in power feared his great appointment and changed him to prefect of Guang and military commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power feared his advancement and transferred him to Guang prefect and Lingnan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五管為南詔蠻所擾，天下征兵，時有龐勛之亂，不暇邊事。

translations.literal: The Five Circuits were harassed by Nanzhao barbarians; the empire raised troops, and at the time there was also the Pang Xun rebellion, so border affairs could not be attended to.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Circuits were harassed by Nanzhao; the empire raised troops, and the Pang Xun rebellion left border affairs unattended.

sentences.zh: 從讜在鎮，北兵寡弱，夷獠棼然，乃擇其土豪，授之右職，禦侮扞城，皆得其效。

translations.literal: Congzan was in the command; northern troops were few and weak and tribal peoples were turbulent; he therefore selected local strongmen, gave them honorary posts, and for defense and garrison all obtained effect.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan's northern troops were few and tribes turbulent; he selected local strongmen, gave them honorary posts, and achieved effective defense.

sentences.zh: 雖郡邑屢陷，而交、廣晏然。

translations.literal: Although prefectures and counties fell repeatedly, Jiaozhi and Guangzhou remained tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Although many prefectures fell, Jiaozhi and Guangzhou remained tranquil.

sentences.zh: 俄而懿宗厭代，從讜以久在番禺，不樂風土，思歸戀闕，形於賦詠，累上章求為分司散秩。

translations.literal: Before long Yizong died; Congzan, having long been at Panyu, disliked the climate, yearned for the capital, and expressed this in poetry; he repeatedly memorialized requesting a nominal post in the auxiliary capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yizong died; Congzan, long at Panyu, disliked the climate, yearned for court, expressed this in verse, and repeatedly sought a nominal capital post.

sentences.zh: 僖宗征還，用為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Xizong summoned him back and used him as minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong recalled him and made him minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: Soon with his original office he became chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became chief councilor while retaining that office.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，盜起河南，天下騷動。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu reign bandits rose in Henan and the empire was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu reign bandits rose in Henan and the empire was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 陰山府沙陀都督李國昌部族方強，虎視北邊。

translations.literal: Li Guochang's Shatuo tribes of the Yinshan Defense Command were then strong and watched the northern border like tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guochang's Shatuo tribes of the Yinshan Defense Command were strong and eyed the northern border like tigers.

sentences.zh: 屬靈州防禦使段文楚軍儲不繼，郡兵乏食，乃密引沙陀部攻城，殺文楚，遂據振武軍雲、朔等州。

translations.literal: At the time Duan Wenchu, defense commissioner of Lingzhou, could not supply his army stores and the command troops lacked food; he secretly led Shatuo tribes to attack the city, killed Wenchu, and then occupied Zhenwu and the prefectures of Yun and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenchu of Lingzhou could not supply stores and troops lacked food; he secretly led Shatuo to attack the city, killed Wenchu, and occupied Zhenwu and Yun and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 又令其子克章、克用大合諸部，南侵忻、代。

translations.literal: He also ordered his sons Kezhang and Keyong to gather the tribes in great array and invade south into Xin and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered sons Kezhang and Keyong to gather tribes and invade south into Xin and Dai.

sentences.zh: 前帥竇瀚、李侃、李蔚相繼以重臣鎮並部，皆不能遏。

translations.literal: Former commissioners Dou Han, Li Kan, and Li Wei in succession, as important ministers governing Bing, all could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Former commissioners Dou Han, Li Kan, and Li Wei, though important ministers governing Bing, could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 俄而康傳圭為三軍所殺，軍士益驕，矜功責賞，勸為噪聚。

translations.literal: Before long Kang Chuanui was killed by the three armies; the soldiers grew more arrogant, boasted of merit and demanded rewards, and urged riotous assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kang Chuanui was killed by the armies; soldiers grew arrogant, demanded rewards, and urged riot.

sentences.zh: 加以河南、河北七道兵帥，雲合都下，人不聊生，沙陀連陷城邑，朝廷難於擇帥。

translations.literal: Moreover the military commissioners of the seven circuits of Henan and Hebei gathered like clouds at the capital; people could not live, Shatuo repeatedly captured cities, and the court found it hard to choose a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Hebei commissioners gathered at the capital; people could not live, Shatuo captured cities, and the court could not choose a commander.

sentences.zh: 僖宗欲以宰臣臨制之，詔曰：「開府儀同三司、門下侍郎、兼兵部尚書、充太清宮使、弘文館大學士、延資庫使、上柱國、滎陽郡開國公、食邑二千戶鄭從讜：自處鈞衡，屢來麟鳳，才高應變，動必研機。

translations.literal: Xizong wished a chief minister to take command in person; the edict read: "Zheng Congzan, Grand Master of the Palace with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Concurrently Minister of War, Commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Commissioner of the Prolonged Resources Store, Pillar of State, Duke of Xingyang with a fief of two thousand households—from the time he stood at the scales of government he has repeatedly come like the qilin and phoenix; his talent is high and his response to change sure; in action he always examines the pivot."
translations.idiomatic: Xizong wished a chief minister to command in person; the edict praised Congzan's talent and readiness to meet change.

sentences.zh: 朕以北門興王故地，以爾嘗施惠化，尚有去思。

translations.literal: "I take the northern gate, the old land where kings arose, and because you once bestowed benevolent transformation there, the people still remember you when you left."
translations.idiomatic: "The northern gate is the old land where kings arose; because you once governed there with benevolence, the people still remember you."

sentences.zh: 方當用武之時，暫輟調元之職，佇殲兇醜，副我憂勤。

translations.literal: "Now at a time when force must be used, I temporarily set aside your role as harmonizer of the elements, waiting until the vicious enemies are destroyed to answer my anxious toil."
translations.idiomatic: "Now at a time of force I temporarily set aside your role as harmonizer, waiting until enemies are destroyed to answer my anxious toil."

sentences.zh: 可檢校司空、司平章事、太原尹、北都留守、河東節度，兼行營招討等使。

translations.literal: "He may be appointed acting minister of works, chief councilor, metropolitan governor of Taiyuan, northern capital regent, military commissioner of Hedong, and concurrently commander of the campaign army."
translations.idiomatic: "Appoint him acting minister of works, chief councilor, Taiyuan governor, northern capital regent, Hedong military commissioner, and campaign commander."

sentences.zh: 」制下，許自擇參佐。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued he was permitted to choose his own staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued he was permitted to choose his own staff.

sentences.zh: 乃奏長安令王調為副使，兵部員外郎、史館修撰劉崇龜為節度判官，前司勛員外郎、史館修撰趙崇為觀察判官，前進士劉崇魯充推官，前左拾遺李渥充掌書記，前長安尉崔澤充支使。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Chang'an magistrate Wang Tiao serve as deputy commissioner, Supernumerary Clerk in the Ministry of War and History Office compiler Liu Chonggui as administrative commissioner, former Supernumerary Clerk in the Ministry of Honors and History Office compiler Zhao Chong as observation administrative judge, former jinshi Liu Chonglu as investigating officer, former Left Remonstrance Official Li Wo as chief secretary, and former Chang'an assistant Cui Ze as disbursement officer.
translations.idiomatic: He chose Wang Tiao as deputy, Liu Chonggui and Zhao Chong as administrative judges, Liu Chonglu as investigating officer, Li Wo as chief secretary, and Cui Ze as disbursement officer.

sentences.zh: 開幕之盛，冠於一時。

translations.literal: The opening of his staff was the grandest of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The opening of his staff was the grandest of the age.

sentences.zh: 時中朝瞻望者，目太原為「小朝廷」，言名人之多也。

translations.literal: At the time those looking to the court called Taiyuan the "little imperial court," meaning how many famous men there were.
translations.idiomatic: Court watchers called Taiyuan the "little imperial court" for its many famous men.

sentences.zh: 時新承軍亂之後，殺掠攻剽，無日無之。

translations.literal: At the time, newly after military disorder, killing, plunder, and raids occurred daily without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Newly after military disorder, killing and plunder occurred daily.

sentences.zh: 從讜貌溫而氣勁，沈機善斷，奸無遁情。

translations.literal: Congzan's appearance was mild but his spirit forceful; he was deep and decisive and treachery could not escape him.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan looked mild but was forceful in spirit, deep and decisive; treachery could not escape him.

sentences.zh: 凡兇謀盜發，無不落其彀中，以是群豪惕息。

translations.literal: Every treacherous plot or theft that arose fell into his snare, and therefore the powerful were wary and subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Every plot or theft fell into his snare, and the powerful were subdued.

sentences.zh: 舊府城都虞候張彥球者，前帥令率兵三千逐沙陀於百井，中路而還，縱兵破鑰，殺故帥康傳圭。

translations.literal: The old command's metropolitan guard Zhang Yanqiu had been ordered by the former commissioner to lead three thousand troops to pursue the Shatuo at Baijing; halfway he returned, let his troops break the locks, and killed the former commissioner Kang Chuanui.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan guard Zhang Yanqiu had been ordered to pursue Shatuo at Baijing; halfway he returned, let troops break locks, and killed commissioner Kang Chuanui.

sentences.zh: 及從讜至，搜索其魁誅之。

translations.literal: When Congzan arrived he searched out the ringleaders and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Congzan arrived he found the ringleaders and executed them.

sentences.zh: 知彥球意善，有方略，召之開喻，坦然無疑，悉以兵柄委之。

translations.literal: Knowing Yanqiu's intent was good and he had strategy, Congzan summoned him, spoke openly without suspicion, and fully entrusted military authority to him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yanqiu meant well and had strategy, Congzan summoned him, spoke openly, and entrusted all military authority to him.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，李鈞、李涿繼率本道之師出雁門，為沙陀所敗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangming, Li Jun and Li Zhuo in succession led the circuit's troops out through Yanmen and were defeated by the Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangming, Li Jun and Li Zhuo led circuit troops through Yanmen and were defeated by Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 十二月，黃巢犯長安，僖宗出幸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Huang Chao attacked Chang'an and Xizong fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Huang Chao attacked Chang'an and Xizong fled.

sentences.zh: 傳詔謂從讜曰：「卿誌安封域，權總戎麾，夷夏具瞻，社稷全賴。

translations.literal: An transmitted edict said to Congzan: "Your will is to secure the frontier and you broadly command the army; barbarian and Chinese alike look to you, and the altars of state wholly rely on you."
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted edict told Congzan the altars of state wholly relied on him.

sentences.zh: 今月五日，草賊黃巢奔沖；

translations.literal: "On the fifth day of this month the grass-bandit Huang Chao rushed upon the palace;"
translations.idiomatic: "On the fifth of this month the bandit Huang Chao rushed the palace;"

sentences.zh: 十六日，駐蹕梁、漢。

translations.literal: "on the sixteenth the imperial carriage halted at Liang and Han."
translations.idiomatic: "on the sixteenth the imperial carriage halted at Liang and Han."

sentences.zh: 上慚九廟，下愧萬方。

translations.literal: "Above I am ashamed before the nine temples; below I am ashamed before the myriad regions."
translations.idiomatic: "Above I shame the nine temples; below I shame the myriad regions."

sentences.zh: 籓閫乍聞，痛憤應切。

translations.literal: "When the frontier command first heard, pain and indignation should be acute."
translations.idiomatic: "When the frontier first heard, pain and indignation should be acute."

sentences.zh: 專差供奉官劉全及往彼慰喻。

translations.literal: "I specially dispatch the palace attendant Liu Quanji to go there to comfort and instruct."
translations.idiomatic: "I dispatch palace attendant Liu Quanji to comfort you."

sentences.zh: 卿宜差點本道兵士，酌量多少，付北面副招討使諸葛爽，俾令入援。

translations.literal: "You should dispatch soldiers of this circuit in appropriate numbers to the northern deputy campaign commander Zhuge Shuang, so that he may lead them in aid."
translations.idiomatic: "Dispatch appropriate numbers of this circuit's troops to Zhuge Shuang for aid."

sentences.zh: 」從讜承詔雪涕，團結戎伍，遣牙將論安、後院軍使硃玫率步騎五千，從諸葛爽入關赴難。

translations.literal: Congzan received the edict with tears like snow, gathered troops, and dispatched牙将 Lun An and rear-guard commander Zhu Mei with five thousand infantry and cavalry to follow Zhuge Shuang into the passes to relieve the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan wept, gathered troops, and sent Lun An and Zhu Mei with five thousand men to follow Zhuge Shuang into the passes.

sentences.zh: 時中和元年五月也。

translations.literal: It was the fifth month of the first year of Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: It was the fifth month of Zhonghe year 1.

sentences.zh: 論安軍次離石。

translations.literal: Lun An's army halted at Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Lun An's army halted at Lishi.

sentences.zh: 是月，沙陀李克用軍奄至，營於汾東，稱奉詔赴難入關。

translations.literal: That month Li Keyong's Shatuo army suddenly arrived and camped east of Fen, claiming to follow an edict to relieve the crisis and enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Keyong's Shatuo army arrived and camped east of Fen, claiming an edict to relieve the crisis and enter the passes.

sentences.zh: 從讜具廩餼犒勞，信宿不發。

translations.literal: Congzan fully supplied grain and provisions to reward and comfort them, but after two nights they still did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan supplied grain and provisions to reward them, but after two nights they still did not depart.

sentences.zh: 克用傅城而呼曰：「本軍將南下，欲與相公面言。

translations.literal: Keyong approached the wall and called out, "This army is about to go south and wishes to speak with the chief minister face to face."
translations.idiomatic: Keyong approached the wall and called, "This army is going south and wishes to speak with the chief minister face to face."

sentences.zh: 」從讜登城謂之曰：「僕射父子，咸通以來，舊激忠義，血戰為國，天下之人受賜。

translations.literal: Congzan ascended the wall and said to him, "Vice Commissioner, father and son—from Xiantong onward you have long stirred loyal righteousness and fought in blood for the state; the people of the realm have received your bounty."
translations.idiomatic: Congzan ascended the wall and said, "Vice Commissioner, father and son—from Xiantong you have fought in blood for the state; the realm has received your bounty."

sentences.zh: 老夫歷事累朝，位忝將相，今日群盜擾攘，輿駕奔播，蕩覆神州，不能荷戈討賊，以酬聖獎，老夫之罪也。

translations.literal: "This old man has served many reigns and my rank disgraces the post of general and chief minister. Today bandits disturb the realm, the imperial carriage flees in alarm, and the divine land is overturned; I cannot bear arms to punish the rebels and repay the sage's reward—that is this old man's crime."
translations.idiomatic: "I have served many reigns as general and chief minister. Today bandits disturb the realm and the throne flees; I cannot bear arms to punish rebels—that is my crime."

sentences.zh: 然多難圖勛，是僕射立功立事之時也。

translations.literal: "Yet in many difficulties merit is hard to achieve—this is the time for the Vice Commissioner to establish merit and accomplish deeds."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet in many difficulties merit is hard to achieve—this is your time to establish merit."

sentences.zh: 所恨受命守籓，不敢辱命，無以仰陪戎棨。

translations.literal: "What I regret is that having received orders to guard the frontier I dare not dishonor the mandate and cannot respectfully accompany the military banners."
translations.idiomatic: "I regret that having received orders to guard the frontier I dare not dishonor the mandate and cannot accompany your banners."

sentences.zh: 若僕射終以君親為念，破賊之後，車駕還宮，卻得待罪闕庭，是所願也。

translations.literal: "If the Vice Commissioner in the end keeps lord and parent in mind, after breaking the bandits when the carriage returns to the palace I may yet await punishment at the court gate—that is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: "If you keep lord and parent in mind, after the bandits are broken and the throne returns I may yet await punishment at court—that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 唯僕射自愛。

translations.literal: "Only take care of yourself, Vice Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: "Only take care of yourself, Vice Commissioner."

sentences.zh: 」克用拜謝而去。

translations.literal: Keyong bowed in thanks and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong bowed in thanks and departed.

sentences.zh: 然雜虜不戢，肆掠近甸。

translations.literal: Yet the mixed barbarians were not restrained and plundered the nearby suburbs at will.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the mixed barbarians were unrestrained and plundered the nearby suburbs.

sentences.zh: 從讜遣大將王蟾、薛威出師追擊之。

translations.literal: Congzan dispatched the great generals Wang Chan and Xue Wei with troops to pursue and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan dispatched generals Wang Chan and Xue Wei to pursue them.

sentences.zh: 翌日，契苾部救兵至，沙陀大敗而還。

translations.literal: The next day Qibi relief troops arrived and the Shatuo suffered a great defeat and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Qibi relief troops arrived and the Shatuo suffered a great defeat and retreated.

sentences.zh: 初，論安率師入關，至陰地，以數百卒擅歸，從讜集諸部校斬之於鞠場，並以兵眾付硃玫赴難。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lun An led troops into the passes and reached Yindi, several hundred soldiers returned without authorization; Congzan assembled the various commanders and executed them in the drill ground, and entrusted the troops to Zhu Mei to relieve the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun An reached Yindi, several hundred soldiers returned without authorization; Congzan executed them in the drill ground and sent the troops with Zhu Mei to relieve the crisis.

sentences.zh: 時鄭畋亦以宰相鎮鳳翔，與從讜宗人，同年登進士。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Tian also served as chief minister while governing Fengxiang; he was Congzan's clansman and had passed the jinshi examination in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian also served as chief minister while governing Fengxiang; he was Congzan's clansman and had passed the jinshi in the same year.

sentences.zh: 畋亦舉兵岐下，以遏賊巢。

translations.literal: Tian also raised troops below Qi to block the bandit Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Tian also raised troops in Qi to block Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 廣明首唱仗義，斷賊首尾，逆徒名為「二鄭」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangming they first raised righteous arms, severing the bandits' head and tail; the rebels called them the "Two Zhengs."
translations.idiomatic: At Guangming's start they first raised righteous arms and severed the bandits' head and tail; rebels called them the "Two Zhengs."

sentences.zh: 國威復振，二儒帥之功也。

translations.literal: National prestige revived again—the achievement of two ru commanders.
translations.idiomatic: National prestige revived—the achievement of two scholar-commanders.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，代北監軍使陳景思奉詔赦沙陀部，許討賊自贖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year Chen Jingsi, military commissioner of the northern frontier, received an edict to pardon the Shatuo tribes and permit them to redeem themselves by campaigning against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 2 Chen Jingsi received an edict to pardon the Shatuo and permit them to redeem themselves by fighting bandits.

sentences.zh: 由是沙陀五部數萬人南下，不敢蹈境。

translations.literal: Thereupon tens of thousands of the five Shatuo divisions went south but did not dare tread on Congzan's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of the five Shatuo divisions went south but did not dare tread on Congzan's territory.

sentences.zh: 乃自嵐、石沿河而南，唯李克用以數百騎臨城敘別。

translations.literal: They went south from Lan and Shi along the river; only Li Keyong with several hundred cavalry came to the city to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: They went south from Lan and Shi along the river; only Li Keyong with several hundred cavalry came to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 從讜遺之名馬、器幣而訣。

translations.literal: Congzan gave him famous horses and vessels in parting.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan gave him famous horses and gifts in parting.

sentences.zh: 三年，克用破賊立功，授河東節度代從讜。

translations.literal: In the third year Keyong achieved merit breaking bandits and was appointed military commissioner of Hedong in Congzan's place.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Keyong achieved merit and was appointed Hedong military commissioner in Congzan's place.

sentences.zh: 還至榆次，遣使致禮，謂從讜曰：「予家尊在雁門，且還覲省。

translations.literal: Returning to Yuci he sent envoys with courtesy, saying to Congzan, "My father is at Yanmen and I must return to visit him."
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Yuci he sent envoys saying, "My father is at Yanmen and I must return to visit him."

sentences.zh: 相公徐治行裝，勿遽首途。

translations.literal: "The chief minister may slowly prepare his baggage; do not hurry on the road."
translations.idiomatic: "The chief minister may slowly prepare his baggage; do not hurry on the road."

sentences.zh: 」從讜承詔，即日牒監軍使周從寓請知兵馬留後事。

translations.literal: Congzan received the edict and that same day sent a dispatch to military commissioner Zhou Congyu requesting charge of military affairs as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan received the edict and that day asked military commissioner Zhou Congyu to handle military affairs as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 書記劉崇魯知觀察留後事，戒之曰：「俟面李公，按籍而還。」

translations.literal: Chief secretary Liu Chonglu handled observation affairs as acting commissioner and admonished him, saying, "Wait until you face Lord Li and return according to the registers."
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary Liu Chonglu handled observation affairs and admonished him to wait until facing Lord Li and returning according to registers.

sentences.zh: 五月十五日，從讜離太原。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the fifth month Congzan left Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the fifth month Congzan left Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時京城雖復，車駕未還，道途多寇。

translations.literal: At the time although the capital had been recovered, the imperial carriage had not returned and bandits were many on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Although the capital had been recovered, the throne had not returned and bandits were many on the roads.

sentences.zh: 行次絳州，唐彥謙為刺史，留駐數月。

translations.literal: Stopping at Jiangzhou, Tang Yanzhi was prefect and detained him for several months.
translations.idiomatic: Stopping at Jiangzhou, where Tang Yanzhi was prefect, he was detained for several months.

sentences.zh: 冬，詔使追赴行在，復輔政，歷司空、司徒，正拜侍中。

translations.literal: In winter an edict envoy pursued him to the imperial camp; he again served as chief minister, passing through minister of works and grand mentor, and was formally appointed palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In winter an edict envoy summoned him to the imperial camp; he again served as chief minister, rose through minister of works and grand mentor, and was formally appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 光啟末，固辭機務，以疾還第。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangqi he firmly declined critical affairs and returned home because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Guangqi he declined critical affairs and returned home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 有司謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: The responsible offices gave the posthumous title Literary and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices gave the posthumous title Literary and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 從讜知人善任，性不驕矜，故所至有聲績。

translations.literal: Congzan knew men and employed them well; his nature was not arrogant, and therefore wherever he went he had reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan knew men and employed them well; he was not arrogant, and wherever he went he won reputation and achievement.

sentences.zh: 在太原時，大將張彥球強傑難制，前後帥守以疑間貽釁，故軍旅不寧。

translations.literal: At Taiyuan the great general Zhang Yanqiu was fierce and hard to control; former commissioners and guards used suspicion to create trouble, so the army was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan Zhang Yanqiu was fierce and hard to control; former commissioners used suspicion to create trouble and the army was unsettled.

sentences.zh: 及從讜撫封四年，知其才用可委，開懷任遇，得其死力。

translations.literal: When Congzan governed and comforted for four years he knew Yanqiu's talent could be entrusted; he opened his heart and employed him and obtained his utmost effort unto death.
translations.idiomatic: When Congzan governed for four years he knew Yanqiu's talent could be entrusted; he employed him openly and won his utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故抗虜全城，多彥球之效也。

translations.literal: Therefore in resisting barbarians and preserving the whole city much was Yanqiu's effect.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in resisting barbarians and preserving the city much was Yanqiu's doing.

sentences.zh: 累奏為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized that Yanqiu be made campaign administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized that Yanqiu be made campaign administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 及再秉政，用為金吾將軍，累郡刺史。

translations.literal: When he again held government he used Yanqiu as general of the imperial guards and repeatedly as prefect of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When he again held government he used Yanqiu as general of the imperial guards and as prefect of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 在絳州時，彥謙判官陸扆嗜學有才思，寓於郡齋，日與之談宴，無間先後。

translations.literal: At Jiangzhou, Yanzhi's administrative aide Lu Yi loved learning and had talent; he lodged in the commandery offices and daily feasted and talked with Congzan without regard to precedence.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou, Yanzhi's aide Lu Yi loved learning; he lodged in the offices and daily talked with Congzan without regard to precedence.

sentences.zh: 乃稱之於朝，位至清顯。

translations.literal: Congzan praised him at court and he reached eminent clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan praised him at court and he rose to eminent office.

sentences.zh: 在汴時，以兄處誨嘗為鎮帥，歿於是郡，訖一政受代，不於公署舉樂，其友悌知禮，操履如此。

translations.literal: At Bian, because his elder brother Chuhui had once been military commissioner and died in that commandery, through his whole tenure until replacement he never had music performed in the public offices—his friendship and fraternal duty and observance of ritual were thus.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian, because his brother Chuhui had governed and died there, through his whole tenure he never had music in the public offices—such was his fraternal duty.

sentences.zh: 國之名臣，文忠有焉。

translations.literal: Among the state's renowned ministers, Literary and Loyal was one.
translations.idiomatic: Among the state's renowned ministers, Literary and Loyal was one.

sentences.zh: 韋貫之，本名純，以憲宗廟諱，遂以字稱。

translations.literal: Wei Guanzhi's original name was Chun; because of the taboo on Xianzong's temple name he was therefore known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guanzhi's original name was Chun; because of the taboo on Xianzong's temple name he was known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 八代祖夐，仕周，號逍遙公。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Jiong served Zhou and was called the Free-and-Easy Duke.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Jiong served Zhou and was called the Free-and-Easy Duke.

sentences.zh: 父肇，官至吏部侍郎，有重名於時。

translations.literal: His father Zhao reached vice minister of personnel and had a heavy reputation in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao rose to vice minister of personnel and had a heavy reputation in his age.

sentences.zh: 貫之即其第二子。

translations.literal: Guanzhi was his second son.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi was his second son.

sentences.zh: 少舉進士。

translations.literal: In youth he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，登賢良科，授校書郎。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan he passed the erudite examination and was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he passed the erudite examination and was appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，從調判入等，再轉長安縣丞。

translations.literal: When his term ended he followed regular transfer and was judged top class, and was transferred twice to assistant magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was judged top class in transfer and became assistant magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 德宗末年，京兆尹李實權移宰相，言其可否，必數日而詔行。

translations.literal: In the last years of Dezong, Metropolitan Governor Li Shi shifted power to the chief ministers; whether they approved or disapproved, an edict would issue within several days.
translations.idiomatic: In Dezong's last years Metropolitan Governor Li Shi shifted power to chief ministers; approval or disapproval brought an edict within days.

sentences.zh: 人有以貫之名薦於實者，答曰：「是其人居與吾同里，亟聞其賢，但吾得識其面而進於上。

translations.literal: Someone recommended Guanzhi by name to Shi, who answered, "That man lives in the same ward as I; I have often heard of his worth, but I have only to know his face and advance him to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Someone recommended Guanzhi to Shi, who said, "He lives in my ward; I have often heard of his worth, but I need only know his face to advance him."

sentences.zh: 」舉笏示說者曰：「實已記其名氏矣。

translations.literal: He raised his tablet and showed the recommender, saying, "Shi has already recorded his name and clan."
translations.idiomatic: He raised his tablet and said, "Shi has already recorded his name."

sentences.zh: 」說者喜，驟以其語告於貫之，且曰：「子今日詣實而明日受賀矣。

translations.literal: The recommender was pleased and quickly told Guanzhi Shi's words, saying, "If you visit Shi today you will receive congratulations tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: The recommender told Guanzhi and said, "Visit Shi today and you will be congratulated tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 」貫之唯唯，數歲終不往，然是後竟不遷。

translations.literal: Guanzhi assented vaguely; for several years he never went, and after that he was never promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi assented vaguely; for years he never went and was never promoted.

sentences.zh: 永貞中，始除監察御史。

translations.literal: In Yongzhen he was first appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzhen he was first appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 上書舉季弟纁自代，時議不以為私。

translations.literal: He memorialized recommending his younger brother Xu to replace him; opinion at the time did not regard it as private favor.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized recommending his younger brother Xu to replace him; opinion did not regard it as private favor.

sentences.zh: 轉右補闕，而纁代為監察。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right remonstrance official and Xu replaced him as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became right remonstrance official and Xu replaced him as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，杜從郁為左補闕，貫之與崔群奏論，尋降為左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe Du Congyu was left remonstrance official; Guanzhi and Cui Qun memorialized on the matter and Congyu was soon demoted to left suppletive remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year 1 Du Congyu was left remonstrance official; Guanzhi and Cui Qun memorialized and Congyu was demoted to left suppletive remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 又論遺、補雖品不同，皆是諫官。

translations.literal: They also argued that although remonstrance and suppletive ranks differ, both are remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: They argued that although ranks differ, both are remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 父為宰相，子為諫官，若政有得失，不可使子論父。

translations.literal: If the father is chief minister and the son remonstrance official, when government has gains or losses the son cannot discuss the father.
translations.idiomatic: If the father is chief minister and the son remonstrance official, the son cannot discuss the father when government errs.

sentences.zh: 改為秘書丞。

translations.literal: Congyu was changed to secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Congyu was changed to secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後與中書舍人張弘靖考制策，第其名者十八人，其後多以文稱。

translations.literal: Later with drafting secretary Zhang Hongjing he examined policy-examination candidates; eighteen who ranked among the names were later mostly praised for letters.
translations.idiomatic: Later with Zhang Hongjing he examined policy candidates; eighteen ranked among the names and were later praised for letters.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 新羅人金忠義以機巧進，至少府監，廕其子為兩館生。

translations.literal: The Silla man Jin Zhongyi advanced through craftiness to junior prefecture director and used yin privilege for his son as student in the two halls.
translations.idiomatic: The Silla man Jin Zhongyi advanced through craftiness to junior prefecture director and used yin privilege for his son as student in the two halls.

sentences.zh: 貫之持其籍不與，曰：「工商之子，不當仕。

translations.literal: Guanzhi held his register and would not grant it, saying, "Sons of artisans and merchants ought not to hold office."
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi held his register and refused, saying, "Sons of artisans and merchants ought not to hold office."

sentences.zh: 」忠義以藝通權幸，為請者非一，貫之持之愈堅。

translations.literal: Zhongyi, through skill gaining favor with the powerful, had many who pleaded for him, but Guanzhi held firm all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi had many plead for him through favor with the powerful, but Guanzhi held firmer still.

sentences.zh: 既而疏陳忠義不宜汙朝籍，詞理懇切，竟罷去之。

translations.literal: Then he memorialized that Zhongyi ought not defile the court registers; the reasoning was earnest and in the end Zhongyi was removed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Zhongyi ought not defile court registers; reasoning was earnest and Zhongyi was removed.

sentences.zh: 改吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三年，復策賢良之士，又命貫之與戶部侍郎楊於陵、左司郎中鄭敬、都官郎中李益同為考策官。

translations.literal: In the third year the erudite examination was held again and Guanzhi was ordered together with Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Yuling, Left Bureau Director Zheng Jing, and Director in the Ministry of Justice Li Yi to serve as examination officers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the erudite examination was held again; Guanzhi, Yang Yuling, Zheng Jing, and Li Yi served as examination officers.

sentences.zh: 貫之奏居上第者三人，言實指切時病，不顧忌諱，雖同考策者皆難其詞直，貫之獨署其奏。

translations.literal: Guanzhi memorialized that three ranked in the top tier; their words were solid and pointed at current ills without regard for taboo; although fellow examiners all found their words blunt, Guanzhi alone signed the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi memorialized three in the top tier whose words pointed at current ills without taboo; fellow examiners found them blunt but Guanzhi alone signed.

sentences.zh: 遂出為果州刺史，道中黜巴州刺史。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent out as prefect of Guo and on the road demoted the prefect of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Guo and on the road demoted the prefect of Ba.

sentences.zh: 俄征為都官郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as director in the Ministry of Justice and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as director in the Ministry of Justice and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 逾年，拜中書舍人，改禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed drafting secretary in the Secretariat and changed to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed drafting secretary and vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 凡二年，所選士大抵抑浮華，先行實，由是趨競者稍息。

translations.literal: For two years the scholars he selected mostly suppressed flashy display and put conduct first, and therefore the rush for favor slightly subsided.
translations.idiomatic: For two years his selections suppressed flashy display and put conduct first, and the rush for favor subsided.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書右丞，中謝日，面賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice director of the Secretariat; on the day of audience thanks the emperor personally granted the gold-and-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice director; on audience thanks day the emperor granted the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 明年，以本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next year with his original office he became chief councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became chief councilor with his original office.

sentences.zh: 淮西之役，鎮州盜竊發輦下，殺宰相武元衡，傷御史中丞裴度。

translations.literal: In the Huai-Xi campaign, bandits from Zhenzhou stole into the capital, killed chief minister Wu Yuanheng, and wounded Vice Censor-in-Chief Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huai-Xi campaign Zhenzhou bandits entered the capital, killed Wu Yuanheng, and wounded Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 及度為相，二寇並征，議者以物力不可。

translations.literal: When Du became chief minister both rebellions were campaigned against; opinion held that material resources could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: When Du became chief minister both rebellions were attacked; opinion held resources could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 貫之請釋鎮以養威，攻蔡以專力。

translations.literal: Guanzhi requested releasing Zhen to nurture prestige and attacking Cai to concentrate force.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi requested releasing Zhen to nurture prestige and attacking Cai to concentrate force.

sentences.zh: 上方急於太平，未可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor was then eager for peace and could not approve his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was eager for peace and could not approve his memorial.

sentences.zh: 貫之進言：「陛下豈不知建中之事乎？

translations.literal: Guanzhi advanced his words: "Does Your Majesty not know the events of the Jianzhong reign?"
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi said, "Does Your Majesty not know the Jianzhong events?"

sentences.zh: 天下之兵，始於蔡急魏應，齊趙同惡。

translations.literal: "The empire's armies began because Cai was urgent and Wei responded; Qi and Zhao shared the evil."
translations.idiomatic: "The empire's armies began because Cai was urgent and Wei responded; Qi and Zhao joined the evil."

sentences.zh: 德宗率天下兵，命李抱真、馬燧急攻之，物力用屈，於是硃泚乘之為亂，硃滔隨而向闕，致使梁、漢為府，奉天有行，皆陛下所聞見。

translations.literal: "Dezong led the armies of the realm and ordered Li Baozhen and Ma Sui to attack urgently; material resources were exhausted, and then Zhu Ci took advantage to rebel, Zhu Tao followed toward the palace, so that Liang and Han became headquarters and Fengtian had an imperial progress—all things Your Majesty has heard and seen."
translations.idiomatic: "Dezong exhausted resources in urgent attack; Zhu Ci rebelled, Zhu Tao marched on the palace, Liang and Han became headquarters and Fengtian saw an imperial progress—all Your Majesty has seen."

sentences.zh: 非他，不能忍待次第，速於撲滅故也。

translations.literal: "It was not otherwise—they could not bear to wait in order and were hasty to extinguish the flames."
translations.idiomatic: "It was because they could not wait in order and were hasty to extinguish rebellion."

sentences.zh: 陛下獨不能寬歲月，俟拔蔡而圖鎮邪？

translations.literal: "Can Your Majesty alone not grant months and wait until Cai is taken before plotting against Zhen?"
translations.idiomatic: "Can Your Majesty not grant months and wait until Cai falls before plotting against Zhen?"

sentences.zh: 」上深然之，而業已下伐鎮詔。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed, but the edict to campaign against Zhen had already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply agreed, but the edict against Zhen had already been issued.

sentences.zh: 後滅蔡而鎮自服，如其策焉。

translations.literal: Later Cai was destroyed and Zhen submitted of itself, just as his stratagem had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cai was destroyed and Zhen submitted, just as his stratagem said.

sentences.zh: 初，王師征蔡，以汴帥韓弘為都統，又命汝帥烏重胤、許帥李光顏合兵而進。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the imperial army campaigned against Cai, Bian military commissioner Han Hong was made supreme commander, and Runan military commissioner Wu Chongyin and Xu military commissioner Li Guangyan were ordered to combine troops and advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the army campaigned against Cai, Han Hong was supreme commander and Wu Chongyin and Li Guangyan were to combine and advance.

sentences.zh: 貫之以為諸將四面討賊，各稅進取，今若置統督，復令二帥連營，則持重養威，未可以歲月下也。

translations.literal: Guanzhi held that with generals attacking bandits on four sides each levying for advance, if a supreme commander were now set and two commanders made to camp together, they would hold heavy and nurture prestige and the matter could not be settled within the year.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi held that with four-sided attack and each levying for advance, a supreme commander and joint camps would nurture prestige and delay victory beyond a year.

sentences.zh: 貫之議不從，四年而始克蔡。

translations.literal: Guanzhi's proposal was not followed; only after four years was Cai taken.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was not followed; only after four years was Cai taken.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 同列以張仲素、段文昌進名為學士，貫之阻之，以行止未正，不宜在內庭。

translations.literal: Colleagues advanced Zhang Zhongsu and Duan Wenchang by name as academicians; Guanzhi blocked it, holding that their conduct was not upright and they ought not be in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues advanced Zhang Zhongsu and Duan Wenchang as academicians; Guanzhi blocked it as their conduct was not upright.

sentences.zh: 貫之為相，嚴身律下，以清流品為先，故門無雜賓。

translations.literal: As chief minister Guanzhi was strict with himself and disciplined subordinates; he put pure current first, and therefore his gate had no mixed guests.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Guanzhi disciplined himself and subordinates, put pure current first, and his gate had no mixed guests.

sentences.zh: 有張宿者，有口辯，得幸於憲宗，擢為左補闕。

translations.literal: There was Zhang Su, skilled in debate, who won Xianzong's favor and was promoted to left remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: There was Zhang Su, skilled in debate, who won Xianzong's favor and became left remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 將使淄青，宰臣裴度欲為請章服。

translations.literal: He was about to be sent to Ziqing; chief minister Pei Du wished to request patterned robes for him.
translations.idiomatic: He was to be sent to Ziqing; Pei Du wished to request patterned robes for him.

sentences.zh: 貫之曰：「此人得幸，何要假其恩寵耶？

translations.literal: Guanzhi said, "This man has won favor—why must we borrow imperial grace and favor for him?"
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi said, "This man has won favor—why borrow imperial grace for him?"

sentences.zh: 」其事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The matter then lapsed.

sentences.zh: 宿深銜之，卒為所構，誣以朋黨，罷為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Su deeply resented him and in the end framed him, slandering him as factional, and Guanzhi was removed to vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Su deeply resented him, framed him as factional, and Guanzhi was removed to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 不涉旬，出為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days he was sent out as observation commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was sent out as observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 弟虢州刺史纁，亦貶遠郡。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu, prefect of Guo, was also demoted to a distant commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu, prefect of Guo, was also demoted to a distant commandery.

sentences.zh: 時兩河留兵，國用不足，命鹽鐵副使程異使諸道督課財賦。

translations.literal: At the time troops were retained in the two He regions and state revenue was insufficient; Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron Cheng Yi was ordered to visit the circuits to supervise collection of wealth and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were retained in the two He regions and revenue was insufficient; Vice Commissioner Cheng Yi was ordered to supervise tax collection in the circuits.

sentences.zh: 異所至方鎮，皆諷令捃拾進獻。

translations.literal: Wherever Yi went among the military commissioners, he admonished them to gather and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yi went he admonished military commissioners to gather and present tribute.

sentences.zh: 貫之謂兩稅外，不忍橫賦加人，所獻未滿異意，遂率屬內六州留錢以繼獻。

translations.literal: Guanzhi said that beyond the two-tax system he could not bear to impose extra levies on the people; what he presented did not satisfy Yi's intent, so he led the six prefectures within his jurisdiction to retain funds to continue presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi would not impose levies beyond the two-tax system; his presentation dissatisfied Yi, so he had six prefectures retain funds to continue tribute.

sentences.zh: 由是罷為太子詹事，分司東都。

translations.literal: For this he was removed to guardian of the heir apparent and nominal post in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed to guardian of the heir apparent and a nominal post in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 上即位，擢為河南尹，征拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne Guanzhi was promoted to metropolitan governor of Henan and summoned as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne Guanzhi was made Henan governor and summoned as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未行，長慶元年卒於東都，年六十二，詔贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Before he departed, in the first year of Changqing he died at the eastern capital, aged sixty-two; an edict posthumously awarded him right vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, in Changqing year 1 he died at the eastern capital, aged sixty-two; an edict posthumously made him right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貫之自布衣至貴位，居室無改易。

translations.literal: From commoner to exalted rank Guanzhi's dwelling was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: From commoner to exalted rank his dwelling was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 歷重位二十年，苞苴寶玉，不敢到門。

translations.literal: For twenty years in weighty posts, bribes and precious jade did not dare come to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years in high posts, bribes and precious jade did not come to his gate.

sentences.zh: 性沈厚寡言，與人交，終歲無款曲，未曾偽詞以悅人。

translations.literal: His nature was deep and reserved and sparing of words; in dealings with others he had no cordiality all year and never used false words to please people.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and reserved, sparing of words, he had no cordial flourishes all year and never used false words to please anyone.

sentences.zh: 身歿之後，家無羨財。

translations.literal: After his death his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 伯兄綬，德宗朝為翰林學士。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shou was Hanlin academician in Dezong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shou was a Hanlin academician under Dezong.

sentences.zh: 貞元之政，多參決於內署。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan's government many decisions were made in the inner secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan's government many decisions were made in the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 綬所議論，常合中道，然畏慎致傷，晚得心疾，故不極其用。

translations.literal: Shou's discussions often hit the middle way, yet fear and caution brought harm; in his later years he suffered heart illness and therefore did not reach his full use.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's discussions often hit the middle way, yet fear and caution harmed him; heart illness in later years kept him from full use.

sentences.zh: 纁有精識奧學，為士林所器。

translations.literal: Xu had keen discernment and profound learning and was esteemed by the scholarly circle.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had keen discernment and profound learning and was esteemed by scholars.

sentences.zh: 閨門之內，名教相樂。

translations.literal: Within the household name and teaching brought mutual joy.
translations.idiomatic: Within the household ritual teaching brought mutual joy.

sentences.zh: 故韋氏兄弟令稱，推於一時。

translations.literal: Therefore the good reputation of the Wei brothers was pushed to the age.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Wei brothers' good reputation stood out in their age.

sentences.zh: 纁累官至太常少卿。

translations.literal: Xu rose through repeated offices to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Xu rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 貫之子澳、潾。

translations.literal: Guanzhi's sons were Ao and Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi's sons were Ao and Lin.

sentences.zh: 澳，字子斐，太和六年擢進士第，又以弘詞登科。

translations.literal: Ao, courtesy name Zifei, in the sixth year of Taihe passed the jinshi examination and also passed the hongci examination.
translations.idiomatic: Ao, whose courtesy name was Zifei, passed the jinshi in Taihe year 6 and also passed the hongci examination.

sentences.zh: 性貞退寡欲，登第後十年不仕。

translations.literal: His nature was upright, retiring, and with few desires; for ten years after passing the examination he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, retiring, and with few desires, he held no office for ten years after passing the examination.

sentences.zh: 伯兄溫，與御史中丞高元裕友善。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wen was friendly with Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wen was friendly with Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Yuanyu.

sentences.zh: 溫請用澳為御史，謂澳曰：「高二十九持憲綱，欲與汝相面，汝必得御史。

translations.literal: Wen requested that Ao be used as investigating censor and said to Ao, "Gao Twenty-nine holds the censorial net and wishes to meet you face to face—you will certainly obtain investigating censor."
translations.idiomatic: Wen asked to use Ao as investigating censor and said, "Gao Twenty-nine holds the censorial net and wishes to meet you—you will certainly become investigating censor."

sentences.zh: 」澳不答。

translations.literal: Ao did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ao did not answer.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「高君端士，汝不可輕。

translations.literal: Wen said, "Lord Gao is an upright man—you must not treat him lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "Lord Gao is an upright man—you must not treat him lightly."

sentences.zh: 」澳曰：「然恐無呈身御史。

translations.literal: Ao said, "Yet I fear there is no investigating censor who presents himself."
translations.idiomatic: Ao said, "Yet I fear there is no investigating censor who presents himself at court."

sentences.zh: 」竟不詣元裕之門。

translations.literal: In the end he never went to Yuanyu's gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never went to Yuanyu's gate.

sentences.zh: 周墀鎮鄭滑，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Zhou Chi governed Zheng and Hua he summoned Ao as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Chi governed Zheng and Hua he summoned Ao onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 墀輔政，以澳為考功員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: When Chi served as chief minister he used Ao as supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and compiler at the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Chi became chief minister he made Ao supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and History Office compiler.

sentences.zh: 墀初作相，私謂澳曰：「才小任重，何以相救？

translations.literal: When Chi first became chief minister he privately said to Ao, "My talent is small and my burden heavy—how will you save me?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chi first became chief minister he said to Ao, "My talent is small and my burden heavy—how will you save me?"

sentences.zh: 」澳曰：「荷公重知，願公無權足矣。

translations.literal: Ao said, "I am indebted to your heavy trust; I wish only that you have no power—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Ao said, "I am indebted to your trust; I wish only that you have no power—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 」墀愕然，不喻其旨。

translations.literal: Chi was startled and did not grasp his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was startled and did not grasp his meaning.

sentences.zh: 澳曰：「爵賞刑罰，非公共欲行者，願不以喜怒憎愛行之。

translations.literal: Ao said, "Rank, reward, punishment, and penalty are not what the public necessarily wishes to execute; I wish you not to carry them out from joy, anger, hatred, or love."
translations.idiomatic: Ao said, "Rank, reward, punishment, and penalty are not what the public necessarily wishes; do not carry them out from personal feeling."

sentences.zh: 但令百司群官各舉其職，則公斂衽於廟堂之上，天下自理，何要權耶？

translations.literal: "Only let the hundred offices and all officials each perform their duties, then you may fold your sleeves in the ancestral temple and the realm will govern itself—why need power?"
translations.idiomatic: "Let every office perform its duty, then you may fold your sleeves in the temple and the realm will govern itself—why need power?"

sentences.zh: 」墀深然之。

translations.literal: Chi deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: Chi deeply approved.

sentences.zh: 不周歲，以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: Within the year, with his original office he was given charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was given charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋召充翰林學士，累遷戶部、兵部侍郎、學士承旨。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Hanlin academician and was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of revenue and war and chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Hanlin academician and rose to vice minister of revenue and war and chief academician.

sentences.zh: 與同僚蕭寘深為宣宗所遇，每二人同直，無不召見，詢訪時事。

translations.literal: With colleague Xiao Zhi he was deeply favored by Xuanzong; whenever the two were on duty together they were invariably summoned and questioned about current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With colleague Xiao Zhi he was deeply favored by Xuanzong; whenever both were on duty they were summoned and questioned about current affairs.

sentences.zh: 每有邦國刑政大事，中使傳宣草詞，澳心欲論諫，即曰：「此一事，須降禦劄，方敢施行。

translations.literal: Whenever there were great matters of state, criminal law, or government, a palace envoy would transmit an order to draft; Ao wished to remonstrate and would say, "This matter requires an imperial edict before it may be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: When great matters arose, a palace envoy would order a draft; Ao wished to remonstrate and said, "This requires an imperial edict before it may be carried out."

sentences.zh: 」遲留至旦，必論其可否。

translations.literal: He delayed until dawn and invariably discussed whether it could be done.
translations.idiomatic: He delayed until dawn and invariably discussed whether it could be done.

sentences.zh: 上旨多從之。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent mostly followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mostly followed him.

sentences.zh: 出為京兆尹，不避權豪，亦師璟憚。

translations.literal: He was sent out as metropolitan governor of the capital, did not avoid the powerful, and was also feared by the great clans.
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan governor he did not avoid the powerful and was feared even by great clans.

sentences.zh: 會判戶部宰相蕭鄴改判度支，澳於延英對。

translations.literal: When chief minister Xiao Ye, who concurrently headed revenue, changed to head the treasury, Ao responded at an audience in Yanying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Xiao Ye changed from revenue to treasury, Ao responded at Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「戶部闕判使。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The Ministry of Revenue lacks an administrative commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Ministry of Revenue lacks an administrative commissioner."

sentences.zh: 」澳對以府事。

translations.literal: Ao answered regarding metropolitan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ao answered regarding metropolitan affairs.

sentences.zh: 上言「戶部闕判使」者三，又曰：「卿意何如？

translations.literal: The emperor spoke of the Ministry lacking an administrative commissioner three times and again said, "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke of the lack three times and said, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」澳對曰：「臣近年心力減耗，不奈繁劇，累曾陳乞一小鎮，聖慈未垂矜允。

translations.literal: Ao answered, "In recent years my heart and strength have diminished and I cannot bear heavy duties; I have repeatedly begged a small commandery but sage favor has not granted it."
translations.idiomatic: Ao answered, "My strength has diminished and I cannot bear heavy duties; I have repeatedly begged a small commandery but have not been granted it."

sentences.zh: 」上默然不樂其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor was silently displeased with his reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silently displeased.

sentences.zh: 澳甥柳玭知其對，謂澳曰：「舅之獎遇，特承聖知，延英奏對，恐未得中。

translations.literal: Ao's nephew Liu Pin knew his answer and said to Ao, "Uncle's favor is special imperial knowledge; an audience reply may not have hit the mark."
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Liu Pin said, "Your favor is special knowledge; the audience reply may not have hit the mark."

sentences.zh: 」澳曰：「吾不為時相所信，忽自宸旨委以使務，必以吾他歧得之，何以自明？

translations.literal: Ao said, "I am not trusted by the chief minister of the time; suddenly from the imperial intent I am entrusted with envoy duties—they must think I obtained it by another path—how can I clarify myself?"
translations.idiomatic: Ao said, "I am not trusted; suddenly I am entrusted with envoy duties—they must think I obtained it by another path."

sentences.zh: 我意不錯。

translations.literal: "My intent was not wrong."
translations.idiomatic: "My intent was not wrong."

sentences.zh: 爾須知時事漸不堪，是吾徒貪爵位所致，爾宜誌之！」

translations.literal: "You must know the times are gradually unbearable—this is what our sort brought on by greedy rank; you should record this!"
translations.idiomatic: "Know that the times are unbearable—our sort brought this on by greedy rank; record this!"

sentences.zh: 大中十二年，檢校工部尚書，兼孟州刺史，充河陽三城懷孟澤節度等使，辭於內殿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dazhong he was appointed acting minister of works, concurrently prefect of Meng, and military commissioner of the three cities of Heyang, Huai, Meng, and Ze; he took leave in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong year 12 he was acting minister of works, Meng prefect, and Heyang commissioner, and took leave in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿自求便，我不去卿。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You sought convenience yourself—I am not removing you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You sought convenience yourself—I am not removing you."

sentences.zh: 」在河陽累年，中使王居方使魏州，令傳詔旨謂澳曰：「久別無恙，知卿奉道，得何藥術，可具居方口奏。

translations.literal: After several years at Heyang, palace envoy Wang Jufang was sent to Weizhou and ordered to convey to Ao, "Long parted—are you well? Knowing you follow the Way, what medicines have you obtained? Report through Jufang's mouth."
translations.idiomatic: After years at Heyang, envoy Wang Jufang was to ask Ao what medicines he had obtained through the Way.

sentences.zh: 」澳因中使上章陳謝，又曰：「方士殊不可聽，金石有毒，切不宜服食。

translations.literal: Ao therefore memorialized through the envoy to express thanks and also said, "Daoist masters must not be heeded; metal and stone are poisonous and must not be ingested."
translations.idiomatic: Ao memorialized thanks and said, "Daoist masters must not be heeded; metal and stone are poisonous and must not be ingested."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其忠，將召之，而帝厭代。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty and was about to summon him, but the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty and was about to summon him, but died.

sentences.zh: 潾亦登進士第，無位而卒。

translations.literal: Lin also passed the jinshi examination and died without office.
translations.idiomatic: Lin also passed the jinshi and died without office.

sentences.zh: 潾子庾、庠、序、雍、郊。

translations.literal: Lin's sons were Yu, Xiang, Xu, Yong, and Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's sons were Yu, Xiang, Xu, Yong, and Jiao.

sentences.zh: 庾登進士第，累佐使府，入朝為御史，累遷兵部郎中、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Yu passed the jinshi examination, repeatedly served on commissioners' staffs, entered court as investigating censor, and was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of War and remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: Yu passed the jinshi, served on commissioners' staffs, became investigating censor, and rose to war director and remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗幸蜀，改中書舍人，累拜刑部侍郎，判戶部事。

translations.literal: Following Xizong to Shu he was changed to drafting secretary in the Secretariat and was repeatedly appointed vice minister of justice, concurrently heading revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Following Xizong to Shu he became drafting secretary and vice minister of justice heading revenue.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，充頓遞使，至鳳翔病卒。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned to the capital he was made commissioner of relay stations and died of illness at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne returned he was relay commissioner and died at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 序、雍、郊皆登進士第。

translations.literal: Xu, Yong, and Jiao all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, Yong, and Jiao all passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 序、雍官至尚書郎。

translations.literal: Xu and Yong reached bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Yong reached bureau director.

sentences.zh: 郊文學尤高，累歷清顯。

translations.literal: Jiao's letters were especially lofty; he repeatedly held eminent clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's letters were especially lofty; he repeatedly held eminent office.

sentences.zh: 自禮部員外郎知制誥，正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: From supernumerary clerk in the Ministry of Rites with charge of drafting edicts he was formally appointed drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From rites supernumerary clerk and edict drafter he was formally appointed drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 昭宗末，召充翰林學士，累官戶部侍郎、學士承旨，卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhaozong's reign he was summoned as Hanlin academician, repeatedly reached vice minister of revenue and chief academician, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhaozong he was Hanlin academician, rose to vice minister of revenue and chief academician, and died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：二武朗拔精裁，為時羽儀，嫉惡太甚，遭罹不幸，

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The two Wu were outstanding and finely cut, standards for the age; they hated evil excessively and met misfortune,
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: The two Wu were outstanding standards for the age; they hated evil excessively and met misfortune,

sentences.zh: 倳刃喋血，誠可哀哉！

translations.literal: blades falling and blood spreading—truly lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: blades falling and blood spreading—truly lamentable!

sentences.zh: 令狐中傷，為惡滋甚，君子之行，其若是乎？

translations.literal: Linghu's wound was a blow, and the evil grew worse—is this how a gentleman acts?
translations.idiomatic: Linghu wounded them and the evil grew worse—is this how a gentleman acts?

sentences.zh: 鄭貞公博雅好古，一代儒宗。

translations.literal: Duke Zhen of Zheng was broadly elegant and loved antiquity—a ru patriarch of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhen of Zheng was broadly elegant and loved antiquity—a Confucian patriarch of his generation.

sentences.zh: 文忠致君，無忝乃祖，衣冠之盛，近代罕儔。

translations.literal: Literary and Loyal served his lord without disgracing his ancestors; the glory of robes and caps in recent times has rarely been matched.
translations.idiomatic: Literary and Loyal served his lord without disgracing his ancestors; such glory of office has rarely been matched.

sentences.zh: 韋氏三宗，世多才俊。

translations.literal: Three generations of the Wei clan produced many talented men in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of the Wei clan produced many talented men.

sentences.zh: 純、纁忠懿，為時元龜，作輔論兵，言皆體國。

translations.literal: Chun and Xu were loyal and worthy, tortoises of the age; as chief ministers discussing military affairs their words all served the state.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Xu were loyal and worthy pillars of the age; as chief ministers their words all served the state.

sentences.zh: 澳之貞亮，不替祖風。

translations.literal: Ao's uprightness and brightness did not replace his ancestral wind.
translations.idiomatic: Ao's uprightness did not fall short of his ancestral manner.

sentences.zh: 三代謚貞，考行無愧。

translations.literal: Three generations with the posthumous title Upright—examining conduct, no shame.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations with the posthumous title Upright—in conduct, without shame.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：後族崢嶸，平一辭榮。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The empress's clan rose high; Pingyi declined honor.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The empress's clan rose high; Pingyi declined honor.

sentences.zh: 高風襲慶，鐘在二衡。

translations.literal: High wind passed blessing; the bell tolled on the two Heng.
translations.idiomatic: High wind passed down blessing; the bell tolled on the two Heng.

sentences.zh: 猗與貞公，繼以文忠。

translations.literal: How excellent Duke Zhen, succeeded by Literary and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: How excellent Duke Zhen, succeeded by Literary and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 純、纁文雅，綽有父風。

translations.literal: Chun and Xu refined in letters, broadly having their fathers' wind.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Xu refined in letters, broadly having their fathers' manner.
